Article Title: Britannia Industries Expands Manufacturing in Bihar with New Unit in Bihta
Author: Neehar
Main Body Content:
Britannia Industries Opens New Biscuit Manufacturing Unit in Bihta, Bihar, Creating 1,000 Jobs

The Bihar government has recently marked another milestone in industrial development with the inauguration of Britannia Industries Limited’s latest manufacturing plant in the Sikandarpur Industrial Area, Bihta, close to Patna. This unit stands as a testament to Britannia’s commitment to growing its manufacturing footprint in Bihar, as well as the state’s increasing appeal as a destination for large-scale industrial investment.

High-Capacity Production to Meet Rising Demand

The new Britannia unit in Bihta is designed with a production capacity of 70,000 tonnes of biscuits annually, ensuring a steady supply of Britannia’s beloved products to meet increasing demand. Built at a substantial investment of over Rs 250 crore, this state-of-the-art facility emphasizes Britannia’s long-term vision for Bihar’s industrial and economic landscape.

This plant follows Britannia’s first unit in Bihar, inaugurated in Hajipur in 2011, which has been operating successfully and supporting local supply chains. With the addition of the Bihta plant, Britannia solidifies its manufacturing presence in Bihar, empowering the state to emerge as a significant hub in India’s FMCG (Fast-Moving Consumer Goods) sector.

Job Creation and Economic Impact in Bihar

In alignment with Britannia’s goal to uplift the communities it operates in, the Bihta manufacturing unit will create around 1,000 new job opportunities for local residents. This development not only promotes job growth but also strengthens the surrounding economy by fostering skill development, boosting the industrial supply chain, and stimulating overall economic activity in the Patna district.

Why Britannia Chose Bihta for Its New Manufacturing Facility

Britannia Industries chose Bihta, an area close to Bihar’s capital city of Patna, for its strategic location and infrastructure advantages. The Sikandarpur Industrial Area offers proximity to major highways, connectivity to key markets, and access to a skilled local workforce, making it a prime choice for Britannia’s expansion. This decision aligns with the Bihar government’s vision to attract investments, foster regional employment, and build a stronger industrial ecosystem within the state.

Future Prospects for Industrial Growth in Bihar

The successful establishment of Britannia’s second plant signals a positive trend for future investments in Bihar. With several major players, such as Britannia, Tata Group, and Medanta, recognizing Bihar’s potential, the state is set to become a prominent hub for industries ranging from FMCG to healthcare. The Bihar government’s pro-investment policies and commitment to infrastructure development have laid a solid foundation for continued industrial growth, offering new job prospects and improving the livelihood of its citizens.

The inauguration of Britannia Industries’ new biscuit manufacturing unit in Bihta represents a significant win for Bihar’s industrial sector and economic landscape. This facility, with its substantial production capacity and commitment to local employment, reaffirms Britannia’s dedication to investing in Bihar’s future. It also reflects the state government’s successful initiatives in attracting industry leaders to establish and expand operations, enhancing the state’s status as a burgeoning industrial hub.

Article Title: Why was the glorious title of Magadh changed and renamed as Bihar?
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
The Curious Case of Magadh: A Forgotten Empire

Introduction

Bihar, a state steeped in history, has been the cradle of several ancient civilizations. Among them, the Magadha Empire stands tall, a beacon of power, culture, and learning. However, the question arises: Why did the glorious title of Magadh fade into obscurity, giving way to the name ‘Bihar’? To unravel this historical enigma, we must delve into the annals of time and explore the factors that led to this transformation.

The Rise and Fall of Magadh

Magadh, a region encompassing parts of modern-day Bihar and Jharkhand, emerged as a powerful kingdom in the 6th century BCE. Its strategic location, fertile plains, and abundant resources contributed to its growth and prosperity. Under the rule of dynasties like the Haryanka, Nanda, Maurya, and Gupta, Magadha expanded its dominion, becoming the heartland of ancient India.

The Golden Age: The Mauryan Empire, under the leadership of Ashoka the Great, reached its zenith. Pataliputra, the capital of Magadha, became a cosmopolitan city, attracting scholars, artists, and merchants from across the subcontinent. Buddhism and Jainism flourished during this period, spreading their message of peace and non-violence. The Decline: However, the decline of the Gupta Empire in the 6th century CE marked the beginning of a period of political instability and fragmentation. Magadha, once the epitome of power, gradually lost its influence, succumbing to invasions and internal strife.

The Emergence of Bihar

The name ‘Bihar’ is believed to be derived from the Pali word ‘Vihara,’ meaning a monastery. During the medieval period, Bihar was dotted with numerous Buddhist and Hindu monasteries, reflecting its rich religious heritage. The region came under the rule of various dynasties, including the Pala, Sena, and Mughal empires.

British Raj: With the advent of British colonial rule, Bihar was reorganized as a province within the Bengal Presidency. The British introduced administrative reforms and infrastructure development, but the region continued to grapple with social and economic challenges. Post-Independence: After India gained independence in 1947, Bihar was constituted as a separate state. The name ‘Bihar’ was officially adopted, perhaps reflecting the region’s religious and cultural identity.

Why Magadh Was Forgotten

Several factors contributed to the fading of the name Magadh:

Political Changes: The political landscape of India underwent significant transformations over centuries. The rise and fall of empires, the emergence of new kingdoms, and the colonial era led to the dilution of regional identities, including Magadh. Cultural Shifts: The cultural landscape of India also evolved over time. The decline of Buddhism and the rise of Hinduism led to a shift in religious and cultural practices. The focus on new centers of power and culture further marginalized the legacy of Magadh. Historical Neglect: The historical significance of Magadh, particularly its role in the development of Indian civilization, was often overlooked or underappreciated. The focus on more recent historical events and colonial history overshadowed the rich heritage of ancient India, including Magadh.

Reviving the Legacy of Magadh

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in reviving the legacy of Magadh. Efforts are being made to promote historical tourism, archaeological research, and cultural preservation. The state government of Bihar has undertaken various initiatives to highlight the region’s ancient heritage, including the restoration of historical sites and the development of heritage tourism circuits.

Conclusion

While the name Magadh may have faded from the mainstream consciousness, its historical and cultural significance endures. The region’s rich legacy continues to inspire and fascinate, reminding us of the golden age of ancient India. By understanding the factors that led to the transformation of Magadh into Bihar, we can appreciate the complex interplay of history, culture, and politics that shaped the Indian subcontinent.

Article Title: Unveiling the Lost Glory: India-Nepal’s Hidden Treasure and Shared Cultural Heritage Resurfaces in Simraungarh
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Imagine a treasure trove buried under centuries of history, waiting to reveal tales of glory, power, and a shared legacy. Welcome to Simraungarh, a site that bridges India and Nepal through its rich cultural and historical heritage.

For decades, Simraungarh remained a forgotten relic of the Karnat Dynasty (1097-1323 CE), a golden age of the Tirhut-Mithila region. But now, after a 30-year hiatus, Nepal’s Department of Archaeology has unearthed astonishing finds, reigniting global interest in this shared legacy.

A Monumental Discovery in Simraungarh

From November 21 to December 11, 2024, excavations at Hariharpur village unearthed an astounding array of artifacts. These include significant remnants of the Karnat Dynasty, including:

Gold ornaments from Khajani Tole. Sculptures of Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Durga, and Krishna in the distinctive Karnat style. Remnants of Tulja Bhawani’s temple, the revered deity of the Karnat Dynasty.

These finds offer irrefutable proof of the intertwined cultural heritage of India and Nepal.

Karnat Dynasty: A Golden Era

Simraungarh’s reign began in 1097 CE when Nanyadeva established dominance with the support of the Chalukya ruler Vikramaditya. The dynasty’s influence spanned from the Mahananda River in the east to the Gandak River in the west, from the Himalayas in the north to the Ganges in the south. This era is celebrated as the zenith of Tirhut-Mithila’s cultural and political achievements.

Shared Heritage, Shared Responsibility

The unearthed sculptures and inscriptions debunk earlier claims attributing them to the Pala period. Experts now affirm these artifacts as Karnat creations, emphasizing the complementary cultural ties between India and Nepal. However, neglect threatens this invaluable heritage. As locals recount, countless artifacts discovered during pond excavations or construction projects have been lost or ignored.

Reviving a Forgotten Legacy

Key figures like Umesh Kushwaha, D.K. Singh, and Bharat Shah have been pivotal in preserving these relics. Their efforts shed light on the Karnat temples, palaces, forts, and sculptures scattered across Simraungarh, which once served as a gateway to this magnificent dynasty.

The 2018 discovery of a Shivling and inscriptions in Tirhuta script and the 2023 unearthing of a six-foot Chaturmukhi Brahma statue underscore the region’s untapped potential. It’s time for both nations to unite in safeguarding this shared heritage.

Simraungarh’s revival isn’t just an archaeological endeavor; it’s a cultural renaissance. Let’s ensure these stories of unity and legacy echo across borders.

Article Title: Siwan Emerges as Bihar's Leader in Overseas Aspirations, with Gopalganj and Patna Following Close Behind
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Dreaming big and reaching new heights, Bihar shines in the latest Passport Service report of 2024. Leading the charge is Siwan, setting an example of ambition and determination as the district tops the state in passport applications and issuances.

The Ministry of External Affairs reveals a remarkable milestone: Bihar issued 402,045 passports in 2024, a 4.5% increase from the previous year. Among the 422,914 applications received, 30% came from just three districts—Siwan, Gopalganj, and Patna.

1️⃣ Siwan: The frontrunner in sending people abroad. 2️⃣ Gopalganj: A close second with a surge in demand. 3️⃣ Patna: Securing the third spot as the state capital.

In the last year, over 500 complaints were filed across Bihar, highlighting instances of deceit in passport issuance and overseas job placements.

Innovations in Passport Services

Bihar’s passport ecosystem is evolving rapidly:

Police verification is now streamlined through the mPassport app, aiming to issue passports within a week. Post Office Passport Seva Kendras (POPSK) have expanded to 35 centers across 40 Lok Sabha constituencies.

New centers for 2025 are planned in Rajnagar (Jhanjharpur), Bhakhra (Vaishali), and Ram Nagar (Valmikinagar), ensuring greater accessibility.

Faster Clearance for Police Certificates

Police Clearance Certificates (PCCs) are integral to passport processing. On average, Bihar takes 12 days for PCC issuance. However, districts like Khagaria (5 days) and Nalanda (6 days) have set benchmarks for efficiency.

Empowering Applicants Through Feedback

Each month, the Regional Passport Office addresses the concerns of over 5,000 applicants via in-person meetings, social media platforms, email, and postal correspondence.

Article Title: Exploring Oil and Gas Reserves in Bihar: Survey from Bhojpur to Sitapur
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Exciting Oil and Gas Reserves Discovery in Bihar: A Game-Changer for the State

Bihar might be on the brink of an oil and gas revolution. Imagine the state’s vast riverbanks and unexplored land holding untapped resources beneath its surface. Could Bihar be the next hub for oil and gas production in India? The government and private players are now digging deep into this possibility.

In a groundbreaking move, Alpha Geo, a private company specializing in seismic surveys, has embarked on a detailed survey covering a large swath of land from Bhojpur in Bihar to Sitapur in Uttar Pradesh. This survey is part of a larger mission aimed at identifying potential reserves of oil and gas along the Ganga Basin, a region teeming with possibility.

What’s Happening on the Ground?

The survey will be conducted using cutting-edge technology, including small-scale explosive drilling and sensors to capture seismic waves. These waves will provide invaluable data to map the sub-surface, pinpointing areas rich in oil and gas reserves. In a crucial step towards ensuring a smooth survey process, Alpha Geo has reached out to the local district police chiefs for security arrangements. This is essential as some minor explosions will be used to dig holes for data collection. The safety of the local communities and the peaceful conduct of the survey is a top priority.

Alpha Geo has already made its mark as the first Indian private company to carry out seismic surveys for oil and gas exploration. Their operations, in partnership with Oil India Limited, are expected to span across multiple districts, from Sitapur to Basti, Gorakhpur, Mew, and finally reaching Bhojpur. The survey’s outcome will be processed using advanced software to generate detailed images of the Earth’s sub-surface, highlighting regions with oil and gas potential.

What Happens After the Survey?

Once the survey is complete, a detailed report will be generated. This report will identify areas that show signs of containing oil and gas. If the findings are promising, the next steps for resource extraction will be mapped out. The development of these resources could be a game-changer for Bihar, generating employment and driving the state’s economy forward.

Article Title: BPSC Re-Examination Today Amid Protests: All Eyes on Patna as Security Tightens
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
When exams determine futures, fairness is non-negotiable. Today, the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) is conducting a re-examination for 12,000 candidates in Patna, following serious allegations of irregularities during the December 13 exam. This crucial step aims to restore trust amidst mounting protests and heightened security.

Why the Re-Examination?

The re-exam specifically addresses concerns about the December test conducted at Bapu Pariksha Parisar, where procedural lapses were reported. Authorities have now split the candidates across 22 centres in Patna to ensure better management and transparency.

Unprecedented Security Measures

In a bid to prevent disruptions, Patna District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar has invoked Section 163 of the Criminal Procedure Code. This bans public gatherings of more than five people within a 100-metre radius of the exam centres. Demonstrations, processions, and even the use of loudspeakers are prohibited.

The restrictions will remain in effect from 8 AM to 5 PM today, particularly impacting prominent centres like P.N. Anglo Sanskrit High School and Government Girls High Secondary School in Shastri Nagar. Candidates are barred from carrying mobile phones or smart devices, ensuring that the examination environment remains secure.

The Protests Continue

Despite these efforts, discontent brews. On Friday, thousands of students took to the streets, disrupting rail and road traffic. Left-aligned student organisations even attempted to march to the Chief Minister’s residence. The protests escalated further as police resorted to force, leaving several demonstrators injured.

Adding fuel to the fire, Jan Suraj Party leader Prashant Kishor has begun an indefinite hunger strike at Gandhi Maidan. He demands accountability from the police and calls for the cancellation of the exam altogether.

A Critical Test for Authorities and Aspirants

As candidates prepare to rewrite their future, the authorities face the challenge of conducting a smooth and fair examination. The stakes are high for everyone involved.

Article Title: Transforming Bihar’s Ganga: CNG Boats to Replace Diesel, Floating Fuel Stations Coming Soon
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
What if the Ganga River in Bihar could be a symbol of clean, green progress? That dream is turning into reality.

Bihar is taking bold steps to reduce pollution in the 448 km stretch of the Ganga that flows through the state. Inspired by Varanasi’s air pollution control model, all diesel-powered boats and cruises will soon switch to CNG engines. This initiative will not only protect the river but also improve the air quality across the region.

Why Diesel is a Problem

Diesel engines are a major source of harmful emissions. According to research, burning one liter of diesel releases 2.6391 kg of carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂). In addition, toxic substances like DPM, SO₂, NOₓ, and hydrocarbons severely harm the environment.

Now, imagine this: over 1,000 boats and cruises in Bihar’s Ganga burn diesel daily. A single boat burning 40 liters of diesel emits over 105 kg of CO into the air each day. The impact on air quality and aquatic life is devastating.

The Green Solution: CNG Boats and Floating Fuel Stations

The Bihar government plans to phase out diesel-powered boats and replace them with CNG engines. This eco-friendly shift will reduce toxic emissions and improve the river’s ecosystem.

Here’s what’s planned:

Drone Surveys: Drones will scan the Ganga for all boats, including unauthorized ones, to create a complete inventory. CNG Conversion: Both small boats and large cruises will transition to CNG engines. Floating CNG Stations: To support this shift, floating fuel stations will be set up at key locations like Patna, Bhagalpur, and Buxar. These mobile stations will ensure continuous supply and can relocate if needed.

Environmental Minister Dr. Prem Kumar shared his commitment: “The Ganga will soon be free from diesel pollution. This move is a big step towards sustainable river transport.”

Why CNG is the Future

Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) is a cleaner fuel compared to diesel. It produces minimal carbon emissions, reducing air and water pollution. Boats running on CNG will help protect aquatic life and create a healthier environment for communities living along the river.

Bihar’s initiative to green the Ganga is not just a government project—it’s a call for collective action. The transformation will begin soon, and you can stay updated every step of the way.

Article Title: In This Region of Bihar, Pan is the Ultimate Gesture of Hospitality – 15 Lakh Leaves Supplied Daily!

The people of Mithila consume so much Pan that every 10 steps you take, you’ll find a shop selling Pan, from bustling cities to quiet villages. You’ll spot people of all ages, from children to grandparents, enjoying sweet or simple Pan.

Why Mithila’s Pan is Special

Mithila’s Pan isn’t just ordinary; it’s special. Locals believe that without the red tinge from Pan on their lips, their day hasn’t truly started. They also associate Pan with good luck and prosperity, which is why it plays a major role in every occasion, whether it’s a wedding, a festival, or a simple greeting.

In Mithila, eating Pan isn’t a one-time thing. It’s a daily ritual. The region consumes 15 lakh Pan leaves daily, which highlights the deep cultural connection between the people and the leaf. Whether they’re children or the elderly, everyone partakes in this tradition.

For the people of Mithila, Pan is much more than a snack. It signifies respect, a warm welcome, and an essential part of their cultural identity. The bond with Pan transcends generations and continues to shape their daily lives.

Article Title: Cyclopean Wall of Rajgir: ASI's Research to Reveal Ancient Secrets
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Did You Know? Rajgir’s Cyclopean Wall Could Soon Join the Prestigious World Heritage List!

Rajgir, a city steeped in ancient history, is once again in the limelight. Thanks to the keen interest of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), the truth behind the Cyclopean Wall of Rajgir is finally set to emerge. This iconic structure, once a protective shield for the ancient city, now holds the promise of revealing untold stories from centuries past.

Under the dynamic leadership of ASI Director-General Vasuveer Singh Rawat, archaeological scientists have launched an in-depth study of the Cyclopean Wall. Their mission? To unearth its secrets and pave the way for its inclusion in UNESCO’s World Heritage List.

A Walk Through History

Stretching over 40 kilometers, the Cyclopean Wall is a monumental testament to the architectural prowess of ancient India. Constructed using a mix of lime, mortar, and natural binding agents, it spans the lush Sonagiri and Udayagiri mountain ranges, embracing the region’s natural beauty while showcasing its strategic brilliance.

According to ancient Pali texts, this wall was not just a defense mechanism but a symbol of the city’s grandeur. With 32 grand gates and 64 smaller entrances, it stood as the formidable protector of Rajgir’s legacy.

Chief Minister Nitish Kumar’s Persistent Efforts

Chief Minister Nitish Kumar has been a vocal advocate for elevating the Cyclopean Wall to World Heritage status. His consistent efforts have now borne fruit, as ASI experts conduct field inspections and collect samples to analyze its origins and construction techniques.

Collaborative Research Efforts

Renowned scientists from the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences, Lucknow, have joined hands with ASI in this groundbreaking initiative. They meticulously inspected the wall, gathering samples that could provide vital insights into its historical and cultural significance.

“This wall was the protective shield of ancient Rajgir,” says Sujit Nayan, a distinguished archaeologist. Its historical importance extends beyond architecture, reflecting the strategic and cultural ethos of its time.

Why This Matters

If successful, this research will place Rajgir firmly on the global map, not just as a tourist destination but as a beacon of ancient heritage. It’s a step forward for Bihar, bringing its rich history closer to the world’s recognition.

The journey to rediscover Rajgir’s Cyclopean Wall is only beginning. Stay tuned as the mystery unfolds!

Article Title: 100 Years of Muzaffarpur Transport: Unveiling the Mithila's First Historic Bus Journey
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
When Muzaffarpur’s first motor bus rolled onto the roads in 1925, it wasn’t just a journey; it was a leap of faith into the future. From connecting the bustling town of Muzaffarpur to Sitamarhi in Mithila, this historic moment, led by the visionary BNW Railway guard Gulab Rai, marked the beginning of a transport revolution in Bihar.

The Bold Beginnings of 1925

In an era when resources were scarce, and the concept of public transport was novel, starting a motor bus service was nothing short of audacious. Operating near the railway station, a central commercial hub, the service initially faced challenges. With a fare of ₹1.8—considered steep for the time—the bus crossed two toll bridges. Limited passengers and high costs led to its early discontinuation. But its brief stint sowed the seeds of modern transport in Muzaffarpur.

The Rise of Connectivity

Post-independence, Muzaffarpur’s transportation network flourished. The introduction of National Highways (NH) and State Highways (SH) positioned the district as North Bihar’s commercial epicenter. Major routes like NH 77, NH 28, NH 722, NH 57, and NH 102 interconnected the district with other parts of Bihar and beyond. This infrastructure laid the foundation for seamless trade, travel, and economic growth.

Before these advancements, rivers served as lifelines for trade and travel. For instance, reaching Patna meant navigating via waterways. However, the advent of railways in 1886 and later roadways revolutionized accessibility, transforming Muzaffarpur into a transport hub.

The Vehicle Enthusiasts of Muzaffarpur

Muzaffarpur has always been a district ahead of its time. In the 1920s, entrepreneur Mahadev Shah brought the region’s first car. This was a time when cars symbolized progress, and buses introduced communities to the concept of shared mobility.

Railways: A Game-Changer

Railway connectivity arrived in Muzaffarpur in 1886, with the Tirhut State Railway linking the region by 1875. This network expanded rapidly, connecting Bihar with key areas of present-day Uttar Pradesh. By 1953, Muzaffarpur became a part of North Eastern Railway, solidifying its role as a transport and commercial hub.

A Century of Milestones

Muzaffarpur’s journey in transportation, from challenges to triumphs, mirrors the district’s resilience and vision. Starting as a single bus route, today, it boasts a comprehensive network of highways, railways, and roads that connect every corner of Bihar.

Article Title: Top 10 Architectural Marvels in Bihar You Must Explore: A Journey Through History and Culture
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Discover Bihar’s Iconic Architectural Marvels: A Journey Through Time

Step into the world of breathtaking designs and cultural richness with Bihar’s architecture—a treasure trove of history, spirituality, and craftsmanship that spans centuries. From grand Buddhist stupas to intricate Indo-Islamic tombs, Bihar’s architectural wonders narrate tales of dynasties, faiths, and artistic brilliance.

A Legacy of Diversity in Bihar’s Architecture

Bihar’s architectural heritage showcases the harmonious coexistence of multiple religions—Hinduism, Buddhism, Islam, and Indo-European influences. Each monument tells a story of cultural synthesis and evolution. Notable features include multi-story structures, arch windows, grand gateways, and moated cities.

Highlights of Bihar’s Architectural Timeline:

Mauryan Era: Known for its enduring stupas and Ashokan pillars, the Mauryan dynasty laid the foundation for Buddhist architecture in Bihar. Gupta Period: Often called India’s Golden Age, this era brought a renaissance in temple art and education, symbolized by the University of Nalanda. Mughal Era: The Indo-Islamic architectural blend flourished, leaving behind grand mausoleums and mosques.

Let’s dive into the Top 10 Architectural Gems of Bihar that define its glorious past.

1. Mahabodhi Temple

A UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Mahabodhi Temple is a beacon of Buddhist architecture. Its 11-meter-high walls adorned with goose and honeysuckle motifs are a testament to its ancient roots. This sacred site, dating back to the Ashoka period, underwent significant renovations in the 19th century, blending history with preservation.

2. Nalanda University Ruins

Enclosed by towering walls and massive gates, Nalanda University is a marvel of ancient academia. Red bricks form the core of this sprawling complex, which houses meditation halls, stupas, and a legendary multi-story library. Explore the grandeur of Ratnasagara and Ratnodadhi, which once stood nine stories tall.

3. Vishwa Shanti Stupa

Nestled on Ratnagiri Hill, this is the world’s tallest peace pagoda, made entirely of marble. Designed by Buddhist monk Nipponzan Myohoji, it features golden sculptures depicting the stages of Lord Buddha’s life. The tranquil surroundings and stunning architecture make it a must-visit.

4. Golghar

Built in 1786 by John Garstin, the Golghar is a granary with a unique beehive design. Its 29-meter-tall structure features a spiral staircase offering panoramic views of Patna and the Ganges. This colonial-era gem blends utility with aesthetics seamlessly.

5. Tomb of Sher Shah Suri

Dubbed the “Second Taj Mahal,” Sher Shah Suri’s tomb is a masterpiece of Indo-Islamic architecture. This sandstone marvel, standing amidst a serene artificial lake, boasts intricate carvings, domed kiosks, and a towering 22-meter-wide dome.

6. Kesariya Stupa

Recognized as the world’s largest stupa, Kesariya stands 104 feet tall. Built in the 3rd century BCE, this Buddhist monument reflects East India’s historical connection with Southeast Asia. Its grandeur continues to attract pilgrims and history enthusiasts alike.

7. Patna Sahib Gurudwara

One of the holiest Sikh shrines, the Patna Sahib Gurudwara is a testament to Sikh architecture. With its golden dome and grand courtyard, this architectural marvel attracts thousands of visitors each year. It is also the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.

8. Maner Sharif

A fine example of Indo-Islamic architecture, the Maner Sharif tomb houses the graves of two famous Sufi saints. The tombs are adorned with delicate carvings and inscriptions in Persian, making it a significant architectural and spiritual site.

9. Barabar Caves

The Barabar Caves are some of the oldest rock-cut caves in India. These ancient Buddhist caves, built during the Mauryan period, showcase intricate carvings and inscriptions. They offer a glimpse into the craftsmanship and religious history of Bihar.

10. Rajgir Hot Springs

The Rajgir Hot Springs, located in the historical town of Rajgir, are surrounded by temples and Buddhist stupas. The architecture around the springs incorporates elements of Hindu and Buddhist traditions, making it a unique fusion of nature and architecture.

Be a Part of Bihar’s Living Heritage!

The architecture of Bihar is more than just buildings; it’s a testament to human creativity, resilience, and faith. From ancient stupas to colonial granaries, these marvels await your exploration.

Stepping inside feels like walking into a historical time capsule, where the aura of ancient India still lingers.

Octagonal Architecture: Unlike most temples with rectangular or square layouts, Mundeshwari’s rare octagonal design is awe-inspiring and deeply symbolic. Tantric Roots: The temple showcases the rich tantric history of India, blending it seamlessly with Vedic rituals. Continuous Worship: Mundeshwari is one of the few temples in the world where rituals have been practiced uninterrupted for centuries.

Nestled amid scenic hills, the journey to this temple is as rewarding as the destination. Bihar’s aviation expansion doesn’t stop at Greenfield Airports:

Article Title: Missed Jumu'ah or Janaza? Pay the Fine—Bhagalpur’s Kurban Village Uses It for a Noble Cause!
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
In Kurban village, nestled in the Jagdishpur block of Bhagalpur, a remarkable tradition has been upheld for over four decades. Every Friday, villagers gather for Jumu’ah prayers, and when someone passes away, the entire village attends the janaza (funeral prayers). If anyone fails to show up without a valid reason, they must pay a fine—a practice that has been in place since 1982.

But here’s the twist: This fine isn’t just a penalty; it serves a greater purpose. The collected amount is used to fund weddings for underprivileged girls, ensuring that no daughter of the village faces financial hurdles in getting married.

How the Fine System Works

The system is simple yet effective. Initially, the fine was ₹250, but due to rising costs, it was increased to ₹500 in 2020. Villagers say that the money has helped in the weddings of over 50 girls so far.

How is the fine imposed? The village head (Sadar) and ten senior villagers take note of absentees. If someone skips Jumu’ah or a janaza, their reason is heard. If the explanation is unsatisfactory, they must pay the fine. The mosque makes announcements to ensure maximum participation. Are there exceptions? Yes! Those who are ill or out of the village are exempted.

Impact: More Than Just a Rule, A Bond of Brotherhood

💪 Strengthening Community Ties

Kurban’s villagers see this tradition as a symbol of unity and respect. They believe that a person’s funeral should be attended by all, as a sign of solidarity and compassion.

🎁 Helping Girls Start a New Life

With over 2,000 fines collected, the initiative has provided financial assistance for countless weddings. This support system ensures that no family struggles alone.

🛠️ Encouraging Social Responsibility

Many villagers say this rule has deepened their commitment to religious and social responsibilities. Mohammad Imtiaz, a resident, shared, “20 years ago, I missed Jumu’ah prayers and had to pay a fine. Since then, I never skip. If I can’t attend for any reason, I inform the Sadar.”

Bihar, the land of ancient heritage, has once again unveiled a rare archaeological marvel— a terracotta sculpture depicting the divine wedding of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. This exquisite piece, discovered in Chausa Garh, Buxar, dates back to the Gupta period (4th-5th century).

Shiva-Parvati’s Wedding Depicted in a Rare Sculpture

Among the numerous ancient sculptures found in Bihar, those associated with Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati stand out. However, the Kalyaan Sundar sculpture from Chausa Garh is unique. It intricately captures the divine wedding ceremony, an artistic representation rarely seen in terracotta.

Brahma as the Priest, Vishnu Performing Kanyadaan

This sculpture narrates a celestial tale— Lord Brahma officiating the wedding rituals while Lord Vishnu, depicted in a rare posture, performs the Kanyadaan (the ritual of giving away the bride). Unlike many traditional sculptures where Lord Vishnu is accompanied by Goddess Lakshmi, this one solely focuses on his pivotal role in the marriage of Shiva and Parvati.

A Masterpiece of Gupta Era Craftsmanship

According to Dr. Shiv Kumar Mishra, a renowned sculpture expert, this terracotta idol is the oldest of its kind. It stands out as most previously discovered idols are stone-carved.

The intricate details are mesmerizing— Lord Shiva is depicted in Tribhanga Mudra, gracefully holding Goddess Parvati’s hand. She, adorned with stunning ornaments, mirrors his stance, creating an artistic symmetry that breathes life into this ancient relic.

Parvati’s Divine Ornaments & Shiva’s Iconic Posture

Parvati’s jewelry—a thick necklace, armlets, and waistbands—illustrates the finesse of Gupta-era craftsmanship. Meanwhile, Lord Shiva’s firm yet elegant stance highlights his divine authority. The sacred fire, an essential part of Hindu wedding rituals, is also visible, making this sculpture a rare treasure.

Similar Sculptures Across Bihar

The discovery at Chausa Garh isn’t isolated. Similar depictions have been found at Murli Pahad in Bhagalpur, Sultanpur, and various sites in Darbhanga and Nawada museums. The presence of such sculptures across Bihar indicates the region’s deep connection to Shaivism and its cultural significance in ancient times.

Ellora’s Connection: A Pan-Indian Artistic Tradition

Experts suggest that sculptures of this theme exist in Ellora Caves, Maharashtra. However, the Chausa Garh sculpture’s terracotta medium makes it stand apart, emphasizing Bihar’s distinct artistic heritage.

A Timeless Legacy of Bihar’s Artistic Grandeur

With each discovery, Bihar cements its status as a treasure trove of ancient art and history. These sculptures aren’t just relics; they are visual narratives of our glorious past, waiting to be explored.

Article Title: 108 Years of Chanting: Swami Santosh Anand Maharaj’s Mission to Save Devagiri Mountain
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
The Fight to Protect Devagiri Mountain Begins

Once a breathtaking range of mountains greeted travelers entering Shahkund, Bhagalpur. But rampant illegal mining destroyed most of them, leaving just a few behind. Among those who witnessed this devastation was Swami Santosh Anand Maharaj, a spiritual leader from Nepal. Seeing the environmental loss, he vowed to protect Devagiri Mountain by dedicating 108 years of uninterrupted chanting of ‘Om Namah Shivaya’. This mission, which began on May 27, 2010, is now a beacon of hope for environmental conservation and spiritual awakening.

A Legacy Inspired by Devotion

Swami Santosh Anand Maharaj’s journey started with inspiration from Pagal Baba Ashram, Jasidih, where a similar 108-year kirtan had begun. With limited resources, only five people joined him initially. But as the movement gained recognition, 20 permanent members took charge, organizing chanting sessions in three-hour shifts. Gradually, the initiative attracted devotees and environmentalists alike, transforming Devagiri into a center for both spirituality and conservation.

A Spiritual and Medicinal Treasure

Devagiri Mountain isn’t just a site for kirtan—it holds ancient medicinal secrets. Various rare herbs like Rudraksha, Kapoor, Long, Hing, Sindoor, Guggul, and Brahmi thrive here. With contributions from Swami Santosh Anand Maharaj and environmentalists like Shiromani, the mountain has become a natural pharmacy benefiting the local community.

The Sacred Temples of Devagiri

Apart from being an environmental and spiritual hub, Devagiri Mountain boasts several ancient temples:

Maa Kali Temple – Located at the mountain peak, beside the chanting hall. Maa Bageshwari Temple & Durga Temple – Situated a short distance away. Baba Girivarnath Temple – A historically significant site, now protected by the Archaeological Department.

These temples, along with continuous chanting, make Devagiri a powerful spiritual energy center.

A Sanctuary for Learning and Healing

Beyond spirituality, Swami Santosh Anand Maharaj has expanded his mission to social service.

Yoga training is conducted at the center. Underprivileged children receive shelter and education. Local residents benefit from herbal treatments. The center also works to prevent further illegal mining.

Veterinarian Dr. Nirmal Kumar volunteers his time, teaching children, while dedicated disciples like Brahmachari Somanand, Om Didi, Shiv Prem, Babita, and Manoj Yadav serve selflessly.

A Monk’s Journey to Devagiri

Born in Patratu, Jharkhand, Swami Santosh Anand Maharaj found his spiritual calling early. As a disciple of Swami Shivanand Tirth, he spent six years in Badrinath’s Himalayan foothills, followed by time in Dhanbad and Nepal’s Jetauranath. In 2010, he finally arrived in Shahkund, where he initiated the lifelong mission to save Devagiri.

Article Title: Simariya & Salempur: 2,000+ Dowry-Free Weddings – A Social Revolution!
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Over 2,000 Dowry-Free Weddings, A Legacy Continued by the Youth

While dowry remains a burden on many families in India, two villages in Bhagalpur, Simariya and Salempur, have set an inspiring example. Here, marriage is not a financial deal but a time-honored tradition. More than 2,000 weddings have happened without dowry, and the younger generation proudly continues this practice.

Simariya and Salempur: Two Villages, One Unique Custom

Simariya, part of Kajreli Panchayat, has around 10,000 people. Salempur, under Chandpur Panchayat, has a population of about 8,000. Though just 4 km apart, these villages share a strong bond. Nearly all marriages take place between families from these two villages, strengthening both familial and social ties.

Simple, Meaningful Weddings Without Extravagance

At a time when lavish weddings with DJs, fireworks, and grand celebrations have become common, Simariya and Salempur follow a simpler approach. The groom’s family arrives at the bride’s home without unnecessary fanfare, and the wedding follows religious customs.

All weddings take place during the daytime to minimize expenses and maintain a peaceful atmosphere. Elders believe that daytime ceremonies help control costs and preserve financial stability.

Elders Set the Example, The Youth Carry it Forward

Village representative Jahir Ahmad states that over 2,000 marriages have happened between these villages, all without dowry. Scholar Maulana Zahid Halimi emphasizes that this tradition has passed down for generations, and today’s youth follow it with pride.

Retired teacher Abdul Qayoom married in Salempur in 1976, and now his son has followed the same tradition. Two days before the wedding, families hold a special ‘Ring and Handkerchief Ceremony’. Around 40-50 people from the bride’s side visit the groom’s house. This ritual strengthens family bonds.

A Dowry-Free Wedding Movement: A Social Inspiration

This practice not only empowers women but also spreads a message of positive societal change. While dowry remains a widespread issue, these villages in Bhagalpur are setting a progressive example.

Article Title: Holi 2025 Date in Bihar: Holika Dahan on March 13, Holi on March 15 – Check Rituals & Timings
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Holi, the festival of colors, is just around the corner, bringing vibrant hues, joyous laughter, and cultural traditions to life! As we gear up for Holi 2025, let’s clear up the confusion around dates and dive into the significance of this grand celebration.

Holi 2025 Dates: Mark Your Calendar!

This year, Holi festivities will take place on:

Holika Dahan: March 13, 2025 (Thursday) – Best time: After 10:45 PM Rangotsav (Color Celebration): March 15, 2025 (Saturday)

Mithila and Banaras Panchangs confirm that Holika Dahan will be on March 13, while Rangotsav follows on March 15. Some regions, like Kashi, will observe Holi on March 14 due to local traditions.

The Significance of Holika Dahan

Holika Dahan, also called Chhoti Holi, symbolizes the victory of good over evil. Devotees light bonfires, reenacting the legend of Prahlad and Holika. According to Acharya Rajnath Jha, performing Holika Dahan during Bhadrakal (inauspicious time) is strictly avoided. The ideal time for Holika Dahan in Bihar is post 10:45 PM on March 13, after Bhadra ends.

Holi Celebration Across Regions

Many people are confused about Holi dates due to variations in lunar calculations. However, here’s a clear breakdown:

Bihar & Most Regions: Holika Dahan on March 13, Holi on March 15. Kashi (Banaras): Holi on March 14. Mithila Panchang: Aligns with Bihar’s schedule – March 13 for Holika Dahan, March 15 for Holi.

How to Perform Holika Dahan Puja?

Take a bath and sit facing the east or north. Place Holika and Prahlad idols made of cow dung on a plate. Offer roli, flowers, raw turmeric, moong dal, betel nuts, rice, and sweets. Worship Lord Vishnu and Narasimha before encircling the bonfire seven times with raw cotton thread. Finally, offer gulal and sprinkle water around the fire.

Why is Holi on March 15, 2025?

According to Acharya Rakesh Jha, Holi follows the Chaitra Krishna Pratipada Tithi, which begins on March 14 afternoon. Since Holi is celebrated during Pratipada, it will be observed on March 15, Saturday in Bihar and most parts of India.

Article Title: Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary to Become Bihar’s Largest Tiger Reserve | 4X Bigger Than Valmiki
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
# Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary: Bihar’s Next Big Tiger Reserve, 4X Bigger Than Valmiki

Bihar is set to witness a game-changing transformation in its wildlife conservation efforts! Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary is on its way to becoming Bihar’s second Tiger Reserve, a title currently held only by Valmiki Tiger Reserve (VTR). The most striking part? It will be four times bigger than VTR, making it one of the largest tiger habitats in the region.

Big Plans for Kaimur: Tigers to Arrive Soon

The Central Government has initiated the process to officially designate Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary as a Tiger Reserve. Starting in May 2025, authorities will relocate tigers from other reserves across India to Kaimur, ensuring a thriving population.

Currently, VTR houses 54 tigers, but Kaimur’s vast expanse will allow the population to grow significantly. The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) has developed strategic guidelines to protect and monitor these tigers effectively.

Eco-Sensitive Zone: No More Industries Near Kaimur

To ensure maximum conservation, the government will designate Kaimur as an Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ). Once implemented, the 10 km buffer zone will prevent industrial projects, preserving the sanctuary’s natural ecosystem.

Officials have marked 450 sq. km as the core zone, where human activities will be strictly prohibited. The buffer zone, spanning 1050 sq. km, will include Shergarh Fort, ancient temples, and historic villages, making it a significant eco-tourism hub.

A 300-KM Wildlife Corridor Connecting Four States

Kaimur’s location plays a crucial role in tiger conservation! It connects with tiger reserves in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Jharkhand, forming a 300-km wildlife corridor. This link enhances tiger movement, reduces habitat isolation, and strengthens conservation efforts.

North: Connects with Sonbhadra & Mirzapur (UP) leading to Dubri Tiger Reserve (MP) South: Extends towards Palamu Tiger Reserve & Garhwa Forests (Jharkhand)

This corridor will help maintain a healthy and diverse tiger population in the region.

The Proof: Tiger Sightings in Kaimur Since 2017

Tigers have roamed Kaimur’s forests since 2017. In 2019, wildlife experts discovered tiger footprints and scat samples. Further confirmation came in 2020, when camera traps captured tigers moving through the sanctuary.

These findings accelerated conservation efforts, pushing authorities to take action.

VTR Tigers to be Relocated for Safety

Tigers often stray from Valmiki Tiger Reserve, leading to human-wildlife conflicts. Now, wildlife officials will rescue these tigers and relocate them to Kaimur’s secure habitat, reducing such incidents.

What’s Next? The Final Steps

The Bihar government has ramped up efforts to finalize Kaimur’s Tiger Reserve status. Officials will submit the proposal to declare it an Eco-Sensitive Zone to the Central Government by March 20, 2025. Once approved, tiger relocation and conservation programs will proceed without delay.

For these pilgrims, this journey is not just a physical one but a spiritual experience. Walking through the same lands where Buddha once preached, they seek enlightenment, peace, and blessings. The sight of monks clad in saffron robes, chanting mantras, and walking barefoot has mesmerized locals, fostering a sense of cultural unity.

Article Title: From Jail to Teacher: Bihar’s Vipin Kumar Gets Government Job While in Handcuffs
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A Scene That Shocked Everyone

The image of a man in handcuffs walking onto a stage to receive his government teaching appointment letter left the audience in awe. The story of Vipin Kumar, a prisoner from Bihar’s Beur Jail, is unlike anything seen before. Despite being behind bars for 18 months under the POCSO Act, he successfully cleared the TRE-3 examination and secured a government teaching job.

Vipin Kumar’s Struggles and Triumph

Vipin, a native of Airki village, Mohanpur block, Gaya, was once a respected teacher at a private coaching institute in Patna’s Saguna Mor. In 2023, he was accused under the POCSO Act and arrested. However, he has always claimed innocence, stating that rival coaching institutes framed him in a conspiracy.

While waiting for justice, Vipin did not let his circumstances define him. Even in jail, he continued his studies, determined to build a future. His hard work paid off when he cleared Bihar’s Teacher Recruitment Exam (TRE-3) and became eligible for a government teaching position.

The Moment That Stunned Bihar

On March 9, 2025, during a grand ceremony at the Mahabodhi Cultural Center in Bodh Gaya, Bihar Government Minister Nitish Mishra personally handed over the appointment letter to Vipin Kumar. However, the sight of a prisoner receiving his appointment letter while in handcuffs left many speechless. For the first time in Bihar’s history, a jailed man officially became a government teacher.

With heavy security, Vipin was escorted from Beur Jail to Bodh Gaya for the event. As his name was announced, he walked onto the stage, still bound by chains. The hall filled with murmurs as people struggled to process the surreal moment. Was this a sign of justice, perseverance, or irony?

“I Want to Serve Society” – Vipin Kumar’s Emotional Words

After receiving his appointment, Vipin spoke to the media. “I have always wanted to educate children and serve society. Even inside jail, I never gave up on my dreams. Once I am free, I will dedicate my life to teaching and shaping young minds,” he said.

His words resonated with many. Should a person who has not been convicted yet be denied a chance at a better life? Minister Nitish Mishra emphasized that the Bihar government is committed to providing deserving candidates their due opportunities. He added that Vipin’s journey could inspire many others facing adversity.

What’s Next for Vipin Kumar?

Despite securing the job, Vipin remains in judicial custody as his trial is still ongoing. His fate depends on the court’s verdict. If proven innocent, he will begin his teaching career. If found guilty, his appointment could be canceled.

The incident has sparked debates across Bihar. Can justice and opportunity coexist? Should someone accused, but not yet convicted, be given such an opportunity? Vipin’s story challenges traditional perspectives, making people rethink rehabilitation and second chances.

Article Title: NandanGarh Festival 2025 – A Grand Revival of Bihar’s Historic Legacy
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
The Grand Comeback of NandanGarh Mahotsav

After nearly a decade, the much-anticipated NandanGarh Mahotsav is making a grand return! The historic town of Lauria-NandanGarh in Bihar is set to host an extraordinary cultural event. District Magistrate Dinesh Kumar Rai and senior officials have meticulously planned the festival to captivate visitors once again. Attendees will enjoy spectacular performances by local and state artists. They will also explore the historical significance of Lauria and NandanGarh. The administration has ensured strong security and seamless arrangements to make this festival memorable.

The Historical Significance of Lauria-NandanGarh

NandanGarh – A Legacy of the Nanda Dynasty & Buddhist Era

Once a magnificent palace, NandanGarh stands as a symbol of the Nanda Dynasty and Buddhist heritage. Historians call Lauria the ‘Mother of History’, tracing its origins to Lohitya Nagar, mentioned in Shanti Awadhesh’s book on Pataliputra.

The ancient Nanda Empire, under Samrat Mahapadma Nanda, stretched from the Shivalik foothills to the Vindhya range. He expanded his kingdom and married Maurya, a young woman from Kushinagar’s Rampur Janpad. Their son, Chandragupta Maurya, emerged as a warrior. As a young commander, Chandragupta led several significant battles, shaping his destiny and laying the foundation for the Mauryan Empire.

The Buddhist Connection – A Sacred Landmark

Lauria-NandanGarh holds deep Buddhist significance. According to Havaldar Tripathi’s book ‘Bhagwan Buddha and Bihar’, Gautam Buddha passed through this region while traveling to Kushinagar for Mahaparinirvana. Before crossing the Ganges and reaching Kesariya, Buddha stopped in Lauria. Here, he shaved his head and declared it his place of enlightenment. His sacred hair was enshrined in a mound, while his followers sent the remaining relics worldwide. Even today, Buddhist monks and devotees from across the world visit Sahu Jain’s ancient mound, offering prayers and circumambulating the sacred site. They also revere the Ashoka Pillar and NandanGarh mound, where Buddhist monks practiced Vedic and Tantric rituals for centuries.

A Cultural Extravaganza Awaits!

This year’s NandanGarh Mahotsav is more than history—it revives culture, traditions, and heritage. The festival will showcase soulful performances by regional and national artists, engaging the audience with music, dance, and theatrical acts. Visitors will also dive into Lauria-NandanGarh’s glorious past, experiencing its rich cultural essence firsthand.

Article Title: Why Bihar’s Litchi Production is Falling Despite Expanding Cultivation – Ground Report 2025
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Bihar’s Expanding Litchi Farms, Shrinking Yields: What’s Driving This Juicy Paradox?

Why Bihar’s Litchi Boom Is Not Translating into More Fruits

Once known for its sweet and succulent litchis, Bihar now finds itself in a surprising situation. The area under litchi cultivation is growing, yet production is plummeting. According to the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, while litchi farming expanded by 3,000 hectares in 2024-25 compared to the previous year, the overall yield dropped by a massive 1.65 lakh metric tons.

This unexpected trend has left many wondering—why are we growing more but harvesting less?

Farming Area Expands, But Output Declines

In 2023-24, Bihar had 36,000 hectares of land under litchi cultivation. That number has now climbed to 39,000 hectares. Regions like Vaishali, Muzaffarpur, and West Champaran, once the strongholds of litchi farming, are now joined by Siwan, Gopalganj, and Sitamarhi, where new orchards are taking root.

Despite this growth, the state’s litchi production dropped from 3 lakh metric tons to 1.35 lakh metric tons in 2024-25. The contrast is stark and worrying.

What’s Causing This Fruitful Decline?

According to Dr. Vikas Das, Director at Litchi Research Institute, one major reason is that farmers are abandoning old orchards. These orchards, although rich in heritage, have seen reduced productivity over the years. Farmers now prefer planting other fruits in these older spaces due to fear of loss and better profit margins elsewhere.

Additionally, low market prices are discouraging continued litchi cultivation. Farmers in Bihar earn just ₹20 per kg, while their counterparts in West Bengal can fetch up to ₹60 per kg. This price disparity has become a real roadblock for Bihar’s fruit economy.

The Sting of a Bug: Another Silent Villain

The stink bug (Sting Bug) has emerged as another pressing threat. Over the last three years, its infestation has been rapid and destructive. These pests cause litchis to fall prematurely, resulting in massive losses.

The Agriculture Department has issued an advisory, urging farmers to use Alato insecticide along with Prahar spray. Timely treatment is crucial, yet not all farmers have access to proper guidance or resources.

New Hope in New Regions

There is a silver lining. With new plantations coming up in Siwan, Gopalganj, and Sitamarhi, the future still holds promise. These regions may eventually offset the current dip in production—but only if pest control, pricing, and farmer awareness are addressed proactively.

For now, farmers are shifting strategies, policymakers are taking note, and researchers are calling for intervention.

Will Bihar’s litchi reclaim its sweet spot in India’s fruit basket? That depends on the steps we take today.

From infrastructure to education, and healthcare to connectivity, this region has become a living example of Bihar’s silent yet powerful transformation.

The Game-Changer: Shri Krishna Setu

Let’s rewind to 12th March 2016, a date now etched in Begusarai’s history. On this day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 3.8 km long Shri Krishna Setu, a rail-cum-road bridge that connects Sahebpur Kamal (Begusarai) to Munger. But did you know the journey began way back in 2001, when Atal Bihari Vajpayee laid the foundation for this visionary project?

After facing numerous delays and hurdles, the bridge finally stood tall—transforming travel and trade across the region. Later, in February 2022, CM Nitish Kumar and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari inaugurated the approach road (333B) that completed the connectivity dream.

Why This Bridge Mattered So Much

Article Title: Begusarai to Get 35 KM Bypass on Budhi Gandak Dam | Traffic Relief on SH-55
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Begusarai’s Traffic Nightmare is About to End — And It’s Happening on a Dam!

Imagine a drive through Begusarai without honking horns, bumper-to-bumper jams, or hours wasted in traffic. Sounds like a dream? Not anymore. A transformative move by the district administration promises to turn this into reality.

A 35-kilometer long bypass road is now in the pipeline — running parallel to the overloaded State Highway 55 (SH-55) — and it’s not just any route. It will be constructed on the Budhi Gandak Dam, offering a smart, sustainable solution to the city’s ever-growing traffic chaos.

Why the Bypass on Budhi Gandak Dam Matters

This new bypass will stretch from Fafaut to Siuri in Manjhaul, running alongside SH-55 — a highway infamous for its daily gridlocks. For years, both residents and local leaders have urged for a solution. Finally, with proactive steps by Begusarai DM Tushar Singla, that long-standing demand is getting addressed.

But there’s more than just traffic relief. Paving this dam-side route not only improves connectivity but also strengthens the Budhi Gandak embankment, enhancing flood safety and disaster preparedness.

Where We Stand Now: Phase-1 Complete, Phase-2 in Proposal

Progress is already underway. The first phase, covering Rosera to Fafaut, has been blacktopped and operational. Now, Phase-2 — Fafaut to Siuri — is on the table. The district administration has formally proposed the blacktopping work to the Water Resources Department’s Principal Secretary, emphasizing its dual benefits: easier transport and a stronger embankment.

A Boon for Two-Wheelers, Three-Wheelers & Emergency Services

SH-55 sees heavy daily traffic, especially from Begusarai to Rosera and Manjhaul. This new bypass will divert smaller vehicles — like two-wheelers, autos, cycles, and light cargo — off the main highway, easing congestion significantly.

Moreover, this stretch could become a vital lifeline for ambulances and emergency vehicles, ensuring faster response times in crises. For local traders and school buses too, it’s a much-needed relief.

Rooted in Local Voices, Driven by Public Demand

The blacktopping of the Budhi Gandak Dam path wasn’t born overnight. Local social activists, traders, and elected representatives have long raised this issue. They’ve highlighted how this road won’t just make travel easier but will also safeguard the dam structure from erosion and neglect.

Now, with administrative wheels turning, the project is closer than ever to reality.

Article Title: How New US Tariffs May Impact Makhana Exports from Bihar
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A Tariff Twist That Could Affect Bihar’s Global Makhana Story

Behind every crunchy bite of makhana lies the hard work of thousands of farmers from Bihar. But a recent development in global trade might just challenge their journey of turning this traditional superfood into an international favorite.

Bihar: The Heartland of Makhana Production

Makhana, or fox nut, is not just a snack—it’s a legacy. Bihar, especially the Mithilanchal region, contributes around 85% of India’s total makhana production. Over the years, this humble crop has gained popularity in international markets, especially in the United States, for its health benefits and unique nutritional value.

In 2024 alone, India exported nearly 600 tonnes of makhana to the US, driven by increasing demand among health-conscious consumers.

New Tariff Policy May Impact Export Viability

According to Satyajit Singh, Managing Director of a leading makhana export firm in Bihar, a recent 26% tariff hike on agricultural imports by the US has raised concerns. Earlier, the tariff on makhana was 3.5%. Now, it stands at 29.5%, which could significantly increase the product’s cost in the American market.

“US importers are requesting Indian suppliers to lower prices by 26% to maintain affordability in their market,” Singh explained.“However, this may not be financially sustainable for Indian exporters.”

“US importers are requesting Indian suppliers to lower prices by 26% to maintain affordability in their market,” Singh explained.“However, this may not be financially sustainable for Indian exporters.”

What This Means for Farmers

The impact won’t stop at exporters. If the US demand decreases, it could affect local procurement rates, eventually impacting the incomes of makhana farmers across districts like Darbhanga, Madhubani, and Sitamarhi. These regions depend heavily on this crop, and any disruption in the export chain could pose serious economic challenges.

Looking Ahead: Diversifying Export Markets

While the tariff presents a challenge, exporters are already exploring new markets in Europe, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East. The global appetite for healthy, plant-based foods remains strong, and makhana still holds promise.

Singh noted,

“This change encourages us to optimize our supply chains and diversify our outreach. India has the potential to build makhana as a global superfood brand.”

“This change encourages us to optimize our supply chains and diversify our outreach. India has the potential to build makhana as a global superfood brand.”

The Bigger Picture: Strengthening Resilience

This development highlights the need for robust trade strategies and support systems that protect local producers from global uncertainties. By investing in processing infrastructure, certifications, and market access, India can help its farmers remain competitive globally.

Progress is finally visible, as land acquisition is now in motion. Farmers from Bankat and Purainee Mauja have given their nod to the project, paving the way for development. The administration is conducting land valuation in these areas.

Meanwhile, for the remaining plots, official notices have been issued. Landowners who haven’t responded will soon see the government taking over their property, as physical verification has already begun.

High-Level Review Meetings Fuel the Pace

To accelerate the project, a review meeting was called by Sub-Divisional Officer Rakesh Kumar, bringing together key stakeholders. Present in the meeting were NH-120 engineer Arya, land acquisition officer Vineet Kumar, and trainee Deputy Collector Amit Kumar.

They emphasized direct communication with landowners and instructed officials to personally visit and resolve issues. The aim is clear—complete groundwork quickly and move into construction.

Railway Overbridges: A Double Bonus for Commuters

Bihar Launches Mega Digitisation Drive to Preserve Property Records Since 1908

Imagine being able to access your great-grandfather’s land deed with just a few clicks. That’s no longer a dream in Bihar. In a historic move that blends legacy with technology, the Bihar government has embarked on one of its most ambitious digitisation projects yet—scanning and securing over 5 crore registered documents dating back to 1908.

Preserving Bihar’s Century-Old Land History

Led by the Prohibition, Excise, and Registration Department, this digitisation effort focuses on preserving property documents that were once handwritten and stored in fragile paper format. The initiative aims to improve transparency, reduce legal disputes, and streamline land ownership verifications across the state.

Completed Work & What’s Next

Tenders have been issued, and agencies are selected for this mammoth job. The goal? To complete the entire process in the next fiscal year.

Why This Matters to Every Landowner

With digitised records, landowners will easily access their title deeds, eliminating the long-standing hassle of physically visiting government offices or relying on intermediaries. More importantly, this move will help resolve land disputes—many of which have been stuck in legal limbo due to missing or unclear paperwork.

Article Title: Jur Sital 2025: How Mithila Welcomes the New Year!
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Jur Sital 2025: A Festival Where Sattu Meets Soul and Water Becomes Worship

In a world chasing modernity, Mithila quietly turns the page to a new year—not with noise, but with nourishment, prayers, and a splash of water on a child’s forehead. Welcome to Jur Sital, the traditional Maithil New Year, where age-old customs create memories that last a lifetime.

What Makes Jur Sital So Special?

Every year, as Vaishakh begins, Jur Sital arrives like a breeze of nostalgia in the heartland of Mithilanchal, located in North Bihar. It’s not just another date on the calendar—it’s a celebration of health, harmony, and heritage.

Families begin their day early. Before sunrise, mothers and grandmothers pour cool water on children’s heads, offering silent blessings for good health and a long life. This act is more than ritual—it’s love, passed down through generations.

Sattu, Aam ki Chutney & The No-Chulha Rule

The kitchen too observes the festival in its unique way. No fire burns on the stove. Instead, sattu and raw mango chutney—prepared a day before—are served with devotion. This traditional fare is not just about taste; it symbolizes coolness, simplicity, and prosperity.

The belief goes: If you eat sattu on this day, your stomach stays cool and your home stays blessed for the rest of the year.

The Two-Day Ritual: From Satuaan to Dhurkhel

Jur Sital unfolds over two culturally rich days. The first day is Satuaan, dedicated to prayers and sattu. On the second day, people celebrate Dhurkhel, where children play with mud and water, reminiscent of a Holi of Earth and Joy.

This isn’t merely play—it’s about reconnecting with nature, touching the soil, and respecting the elements. In Mithila, even games teach lessons of sustainability.

A Festival Rooted in Love for Children and Nature

While the rituals are followed by all, children remain at the heart of Jur Sital. From water blessings to cold meals, everything is designed around their well-being. It’s a gentle reminder that festivals aren’t only about the divine—they’re about the future generation, too.

Just like Chhath Puja honors the sun, Jur Sital honors water and earth. And in doing so, it blends environmental awareness with spiritual depth.

Article Title: Muzaffarpur Receives 10,000+ of India’s Most Advanced EVMs for Assembly Elections

Main Body Content:
Muzaffarpur Gets 10,400 High-Security EVMs: Bihar’s Big Leap Towards Transparent Elections

When it comes to voting, trust is everything. And this time, Muzaffarpur is setting a powerful example. For the first time in Bihar, over 10,000 of India’s most advanced EVMs (Electronic Voting Machines) are arriving from Hyderabad. These M3-generation machines are expected to transform the upcoming Assembly elections into the most transparent and secure yet.

What’s New: The Arrival of 10,400 M3 EVMs in Muzaffarpur

The Election Commission has dispatched 10,400 high-tech EVMs to Muzaffarpur. These machines are not just regular upgrades—they’re a part of India’s third-generation EVM technology. Before Bihar, only Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh had the chance to use them.

By April 21, all the new Ballot Units (BU), Control Units (CU), and VVPATs will reach the warehouse. Preparations are in full swing to deploy them smoothly in the region.

What Makes M3 EVMs So Advanced?

The M3 EVMs boast enhanced encryption and tamper-proof security. Unlike older machines, these can detect any unauthorized access attempt instantly. They also come integrated with VVPAT (Voter Verified Paper Audit Trail), giving voters a printed confirmation of their vote.

Here’s what stands out:

Standalone system: No internet, no hacking risks Strong encryption: Prevents tampering Real-time error detection High data capacity: Handles more candidates and voter details Full transparency with voter-verified paper slips

Standalone system: No internet, no hacking risks

Strong encryption: Prevents tampering

Real-time error detection

High data capacity: Handles more candidates and voter details

Full transparency with voter-verified paper slips

Thanks to these features, political parties and voters alike can trust the process more than ever before.

First Level Check (FLC) Begins May 25

The First Level Checking (FLC) of these EVMs will start on May 25 and continue for 32 days. A dedicated team of 25 engineers will conduct this detailed verification. It’s a crucial step before mock polls and randomization begin.

Importantly, representatives from political parties will also be present during the mock polls—ensuring complete transparency.

EVM Sets Headed to Other Districts Too

Muzaffarpur isn’t the only district to benefit. Around 5,650 EVM sets will be sent from here to nearby districts like Samastipur, East Champaran, West Champaran, Sitamarhi, and Sheohar.

The entire operation reflects a massive shift in how Bihar is handling its election infrastructure this year.

Why This Matters to Every Voter

For the first time, voters in Muzaffarpur will see the most secure voting system India has ever developed. It’s not just a tech upgrade—it’s a trust upgrade. Every vote counts, and now, every vote is verified, traceable, and protected from tampering.

With these changes, Bihar is making a bold statement: clean elections, empowered voters, and zero compromise on integrity.

Article Title: Patna Road Update: Bihta to JP Ganga Path Road Expansion Underway – Full Details Inside
Author: Amrita

Patna’s roads are about to tell a new story—and it begins with Behta to Maner. While everyone was watching the skyways and flyovers, a quieter revolution has taken shape below. It’s not just construction—it’s Bihar, building momentum!

A Clear Route to the Future: What’s Happening?

The Bihar government, under the leadership of CM Nitish Kumar, is accelerating infrastructure projects in Patna to transform urban mobility. As part of this mission, the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for widening the crucial Behta–Maner route is ready.

This 22-kilometer stretch will soon be expanded to 14 meters, connecting smoothly to JP Ganga Path—one of Patna’s most ambitious expressway projects. The move is not just about width; it’s about opening up ease, time, and economic opportunity for thousands of daily commuters.

Big Budget, Bigger Impact

With an expected investment of ₹70 crore, the widened Behta-Danapur-Maner route will boost connectivity towards Ara and Buxar. Until JP Ganga Path extends to Koilwar, this widened stretch will serve as a strategic alternative, helping ease traffic and save hours of travel time.

Moreover, the upcoming Danapur-Bihta Elevated Road will further reduce congestion, marking a new chapter in Patna’s west zone development.

Not Just One—Three Roads Are Set for a Makeover

This isn’t a one-road story. The state government has placed Patna West Path Pramandal in charge of executing three crucial road expansions:

✅Gola Road Expansion

Currently just 7.5 meters wide, Gola Road—connecting Nehru Path (Bailey Road)—will soon feature dual 7-meter lanes. With a budget of ₹20 crore, the project includes proper drainage, dividers, and sidewalks to ease traffic and prevent flooding.

✅ Khagaul–Digha Nahar Road

Plans are underway to turn this canal-side road into a 14-meter-wide four-lane route. At a cost of ₹70 crore, the project requires relocating schools in Chulhaichak and Kothwa villages. Authorities will also remove encroachments and mark land boundaries by May.

Time-Bound Execution with No Loose Ends

District Magistrate Dr. Chandrashekhar Singh has assured timely execution. The tender process is almost complete. Temporary encroachments on government land will be dealt with strictly—legal notices will follow if deadlines are missed.

These aren’t just plans on paper. These are real steps being taken, with deadlines, budgets, and local accountability.

Better roads lead to better lives. From reducing travel time to boosting local business and easing school commutes, these changes will touch every Patnaite’s life. Once completed, these roads will serve as milestones in Patna’s journey towards becoming a modern, well-connected city.

But this isn’t the end—Patna’s infrastructure growth is just warming up.

Article Title: Two-Day Training for Bihar BLOs by EC
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A New Chapter in Bihar’s Electoral Readiness

“Chunav ka Bigul baj chuka hai!”Yes, the countdown has begun for Bihar’s Assembly Elections 2025, and the Election Commission of India is wasting no time. In a powerful move, the EC launched an intensive two-day training and capacity-building programme for Booth Level Officers (BLOs) from Bihar. And this is not just routine—this is a masterclass in democracy management.

Held at the India International Institute of Democracy and Election Management (IIIDEM), the event kicked off with the presence of two powerful names—Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioner Dr. Vivek Joshi. Their interaction set the tone for what’s being termed as one of the most focused training initiatives in recent times.

What’s the Big Deal About This Training?

Quite a lot, actually.

A total of 229 BLOs, along with 12 Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and 2 District Electoral Officers (DEOs) from Bihar, are being trained. That’s not all—a specialized session for the State Police Nodal Officer (SPNO) and other key Police Officers is also part of this packed programme.

The goal?To familiarize BLOs with their responsibilities under the electoral framework and make them tech-ready. The officers are getting hands-on experience with new IT applications that will help in maintaining error-free electoral rolls.

And the result of this training? These BLOs will become Assembly Level Master Trainers (ALMTs)—spreading their knowledge and enhancing the electoral machinery from the grassroots.

Why This Matters More Than Ever

With Bihar heading into crucial elections later this year, the pressure is high. But instead of relying on outdated methods, the EC is investing in smart systems and smarter people.

This session is part of Phase 1 of the physical training programmes and follows the training of over 555 BLOs from Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam. Additionally, 279 Booth Level Agents (BLA-1s) of major political parties in Bihar have also undergone training.

Such steps are ensuring that democracy is not just practiced—but perfected.

Policing the Process: Behind-the-Scenes Readiness

While the BLOs are being trained to ensure electoral accuracy, police officers are being empowered to safeguard the process.

From vulnerability assessments to deployment of CAPFs (Central Armed Police Forces), every aspect is being covered to ensure peaceful, fair elections. Special sessions are also dedicated to the Model Code of Conduct (MCC), ensuring that no line is crossed when the elections heat up.

The Bigger Picture

This isn’t just training—it’s an investment in trust and transparency. The Election Commission is making sure that when Bihar goes to the polls, every vote counts, every process is clean, and every officer is ready.

And it’s not just Bihar—this programme sets a benchmark for the rest of the nation too. A more trained BLO corps today means a stronger, more accountable democracy tomorrow.

Article Title: This Bridge Will Transform the Future of Two Districts in Bihar

Main Body Content:

From Struggles to Solutions: Farmers’ Wait Comes to an End

For years, farmers from the fertile lands of Munger and Lakhisarai have faced immense challenges reaching their farmlands across the river. Carrying seeds, tools, and crops over boats and through unpredictable waters became part of their daily life.

Now, a bridge near Hemjapur is set to change that—connecting Parora Tola to NH-80 and making access smoother, safer, and faster for more than 70,000 bighas of farmland.

Why This Bridge Matters So Much

This isn’t just a piece of infrastructure—it’s a lifeline for villages like Vansipur, Tajpur, Devghara, Amarapur, and Bhidha. These areas are rich in agriculture but isolated by geography.Farmers here grow a variety of crops like parwal, kakdi, kaddu, kheera, maize, wheat, and ajwain—yet transporting them to markets has always been an uphill task.

The new bridge will change that. It will bring markets closer, reduce crop wastage, and open up new possibilities for trade and livelihood.

The Diara Region: Fertile But Forgotten

The Diara belt—stretching across parts of Munger and Lakhisarai—is known for its rich soil. But crossing the Ganga every day made even basic farming activities difficult.

During floods, the challenges multiplied. Villagers had to travel far for daily essentials, healthcare, and safety. A simple trip to the market or a police station required hours of detour or unsafe river crossings.

With this bridge, the region is finally getting the access it deserves.

Local Voices, Real Hopes

Villagers across the region are hopeful and grateful. Dukhan Mahato from Parora Tola shared, “We’ve lived and farmed here for generations, but getting to our own land was always a challenge. This bridge gives us freedom.”Ashish Kumar Singh, a youth from Durgapur, added, “It’s more than convenience. It’s about building a better future—for farmers, families, and students.”

The joy is real. The relief is visible.

From Isolation to Inclusion

The bridge will also benefit nearby areas like Khawa, Medani Chowki, and parts of Suryagarha block, which previously had limited access to basic facilities. It will shorten travel time, reduce transport costs, and ensure that even during emergencies, help is within reach.

One bridge. Two districts. Thousands of lives changed forever.This isn’t just infrastructure—it’s dignity, access, and a better tomorrow for every farmer who has waited decades for this moment.

Article Title: North Bihar to Get Uninterrupted Electricity: 68 Power Substations Under Construction

A Brighter Future Starts with Stronger Power

North Bihar is witnessing a major shift in its power infrastructure. NBPDCL (North Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited) has begun the construction of 68 new power substations that will ensure uninterrupted electricity for every household, farm, and business.

As demand rises due to the growth of industries, agriculture, and households, this project arrives at the perfect moment. These new substations will boost power supply and provide reliable, high-quality electricity.

This initiative provides businesses with the stability they need to thrive and expand without limitations.

Article Title: No More Traffic Jam at Patna Junction – Smart Vending Zone Plan in Action
