Article Title: Meet Amit Dhawal the Patna Founder Behind Stunning Hollywood VFX
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Patna to Pixar: How Filaments Visual Effects and Founder Amit Dhawal Quietly Took Over Hollywood

The untold story of a Bihar-born dreamer who put Kidwaipuri on the global film map

“In the middle of dusty lanes and slow internet, we created Hollywood magic.”That’s how Amit Dhawal, Founder and CEO of Filaments Visual Effects, remembers the early days of building a global studio in Patna.

His journey didn’t begin with a grand office or a large team. It began with belief — belief in Bihar’s raw creative talent, and in his ability to lead them towards the world stage. While others moved away from their roots to chase opportunities, Amit brought opportunity back home.

From Disney’s Color Labs to the Heart of Hollywood

Amit’s career in visual storytelling began in 1996. He worked on Disney’s Absent Minded Professor, where he supervised the complete colorization of the film. That early experience became his foundation.

Over time, his portfolio expanded. Films like Apocalypto, The Golden Compass, Racing Stripes, and The Legend of Zorro carried his touch. His work was not limited to execution; it carried creative depth.

In 2005, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences honored him for his contribution to The Triangle. He worked closely with Emmy-winning VFX supervisors like Marc Wiegert and Volker Engel. Each project further sharpened his craft and deepened his confidence.

Filaments Visual Effects: Born in Bihar, Built for the World

At first, the journey was difficult. Resources were scarce, and infrastructure posed daily challenges. Still, Amit stayed committed. He personally trained his team in rotoscoping, matchmoving, clean plating, and wire removal. As results improved, trust grew.

Article Title: RPCAU Develops 3 New Maize Varieties to Boost Bihar Agriculture & Nutrition
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
“Maize Miracle in Bihar! RPCAU Launches 3 Game-Changing Varieties for Farmers, Nutrition & Markets”

Bihar’s Maize Revolution Begins at Dholi

Bihar is sowing the seeds of an agricultural revolution — and it starts with three remarkable maize varieties tailored just for its land, climate, and people.

In a breakthrough for eastern India’s farming sector, Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University (RPCAU) has unveiled three innovative maize hybrids that are set to reshape farming income, nutrition, and agri-business in Bihar.

These varieties—Rajendra Baby Corn-1, Rajendra Pop Corn-1, and Shaktiman-5—are not just new crops. They are tools of transformation for small and marginal farmers.

Rajendra Baby Corn-1: Quick Income, Dual Purpose

Developed by the maize breeding team at Tirhut College of Agriculture (TCA), Dholi, Rajendra Baby Corn-1 is Bihar’s first region-specific baby corn hybrid. It matures in just two months, giving farmers a fast turnaround crop with 12–15 quintals per hectare of fresh baby corn.

But there’s more—this hybrid also yields up to 300 quintals per hectare of green fodder, making it a dual-purpose boon for farmers with livestock.

“Baby corn has a strong demand in cities and food industries, but Bihar lacked a variety that fits our unique climate. This hybrid fills that gap,” said Ajay Kumar, maize scientist at RPCAU.

“Baby corn has a strong demand in cities and food industries, but Bihar lacked a variety that fits our unique climate. This hybrid fills that gap,” said Ajay Kumar, maize scientist at RPCAU.

With rapid growth and urban demand, this variety is a clear win for farmers seeking both speed and sustainability.

Rajendra Pop Corn-1: From Fields to Packaged Snacks

Popcorn is no longer just a cinema treat—it’s a booming snack industry, and RPCAU wants Bihar’s farmers to get their slice of the pie.

Rajendra Pop Corn-1, specially tailored for Bihar’s agro-climatic zones, matures in just 80–90 days. It thrives in both Rabi and late Kharif seasons, delivering 30–40 quintals per hectare.

Its secret weapon? A popping ratio of 34–36 cc/g and 95% popping success, producing premium butterfly-type flakes loved by snack brands.

For farmers, this means not just yield, but market-ready quality.

Shaktiman-5: Feeding Futures with Biofortified Protein

More than a crop, Shaktiman-5 is a nutritional intervention. This biofortified Quality Protein Maize (QPM) is rich in lysine and tryptophan—two essential amino acids missing in most cereals.

Why does it matter? Because protein deficiency still affects large rural populations, especially children. Shaktiman-5 aligns with national goals like Poshan Abhiyaan, the National Biofortification Mission, and even strengthens food schemes like mid-day meals and anganwadi nutrition.

“This variety isn’t just for fields—it’s for kitchens, schools, and hospitals,” noted RPCAU Vice-Chancellor P.S. Pandey.

From better child development to improved livestock feed, this variety offers high returns with high impact.

Higher returns in shorter durations Suitability for Bihar’s climate Nutrition-led innovation Dual-use crops for income + fodder Strong urban and industry demand

Article Title: Patna Launches Weekly ‘No Horn Day’
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
“No Horn Sundays in Patna: Silence Speaks Louder Than Honks!”

When the city slows its noise, hearts listen better. Patna has taken a bold step towards peace with the launch of a weekly ‘No Horn Day’. Every Sunday, until October 2, the streets will echo less with blaring horns and more with mindful silence, thanks to the initiative by the Bihar State Pollution Control Board (BSPCB).

A City’s Pledge for Peace

The campaign urges drivers to avoid unnecessary honking, especially in quiet zones like hospitals, courts, schools, and within 100 metres of sensitive spots including the secretariat, legislative assembly, Raj Bhavan, and the city’s biological park.

Officials are clear: reducing noise is not just about comfort—it’s about health. Studies show that constant exposure to loud sounds increases stress, disturbs sleep, and even affects heart health. By embracing silence, residents can literally breathe easier.

Awareness Across Patna’s Four Zones

To make the change visible, the BSPCB has divided Patna into four zones. Their teams will visit key spots, talking to motorists and locals about why noise matters. Volunteers and officials will hand out awareness leaflets, while traffic police will encourage drivers to keep their hands off the horn—unless absolutely necessary.

Many citizens already see the difference. “It’s refreshing,” says Sunita, a teacher from Kankarbagh. “For the first time, I could hear birds chirping during my Sunday walk.”

Loudspeakers Under the Scanner Too

The BSPCB has also reminded residents about existing restrictions on loudspeakers, DJs, and public address systems. Without special permission, these cannot be used between 10 pm and 6 am. Anyone breaking the rules risks penalties under Section 15 of the Environment Protection Act, 1986. Equipment may even be seized under the Noise Pollution Rules, 2000.

The message is clear—Patna is ready to reclaim its soundscape. Less honking, fewer late-night loudspeakers, and more moments of calm can turn the city into a healthier, happier place.

For those flying in, the improvements will be just as striking. Better highways will reduce travel time from Patna and Darbhanga airports, making it possible to reach Punaura Dham from Darbhanga in about an hour. Article Title: Patna Launches ‘Har Din Har Gali’ Cleanliness Drive
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Patna Kicks Off ‘Har Din Har Gali’ Drive to Keep Every Street Clean

A Daily Dose of Cleanliness for Patna

Imagine waking up to spotless streets every single day. That’s the vision Patna Municipal Corporation has rolled out with its new campaign — ‘Har Din Har Gali’. The goal is simple but powerful: make every street in the city cleaner, safer, and healthier.

Launched on August 14, 2025, the drive focuses on 100% door-to-door garbage collection, mosquito control, and daily road cleaning. The Municipal Commissioner, Animesh Kumar Parashar, shared that this mission is about more than tidiness — it’s about protecting public health and boosting Patna’s rank in the Swachh Survekshan survey.

Morning Checks, Real-Time Reports

This campaign comes with strict monitoring. Every day from 7 AM, ward nodal officers will inspect their areas. By 2 PM, they’ll send detailed cleanliness reports to headquarters.

Public places will also see lime and bleaching powder spraying to prevent infections. Additionally, anti-larva spraying and fogging will be done regularly to keep mosquito-borne diseases at bay.

Zones Under Strong Leadership

To make things run smoother, the city has been divided into six zones under two leaders. Ashish Kumar will oversee Patliputra, Kankarbagh, and Patna City. Rajan Sinha will handle Nutan Rajdhani, Bankipur, and Azimabad.

These officials will not only inspect work daily but also coordinate closely with ward officers. Their hands-on approach is expected to speed up problem-solving and improve results.

Residents at the Heart of the Mission

The Municipal Corporation knows that a city can only stay clean if its residents take part. That’s why they are urging people to cooperate with garbage collectors, avoid littering, and keep areas around their homes clean.

With this collective effort, Patna is aiming for more than just neat streets. It’s about creating a city that reflects pride, health, and responsibility in every lane.

Article Title: Bihar Energy Secretary Reviews Gaya-Punpun Transmission Projects

Article Title: Bihar Govt to Provide Free Rooftop Solar Panels to 58.89 Lakh Families
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Patna, August 16, 2025 – Imagine a Bihar where every low-income home runs on clean, free energy from the sun. That dream is turning into reality, as the state government launches one of India’s largest green energy missions—free rooftop solar panels for 58.89 lakh Kutir Jyoti (BPL) households.

A Landmark Step Toward Green Energy

The Bihar government has taken a bold leap to make renewable energy a household reality. Under this initiative, every Kutir Jyoti family will receive a 1.1 KW rooftop solar panel—absolutely free.

Energy Department Secretary and BSPHCL CMD Manoj Kumar Singh explained that the government has designed the scheme under the PM Surya Ghar Yojana. The central government will contribute ₹33,000, while the state will provide ₹27,000, covering the full cost of each installation.

The project’s total budget stands at ₹16,000 crore. The state plans to meet this target within two years by using existing subsidy allocations, ensuring no extra financial burden.

Extending Support Beyond BPL Families

The scheme is not just for Kutir Jyoti consumers. The state will also provide financial assistance to 1.30 crore domestic consumers who wish to install solar panels. This wider support ensures more households shift from traditional electricity to renewable power.

According to Energy Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Bihar aims to cut dependence on conventional power sources and accelerate renewable adoption. The goal is clear: reduce bills, boost sustainability, and empower citizens with clean energy.

A Vision Backed by Leadership

During a virtual outreach, Chief Minister Nitish Kumar reaffirmed the state’s commitment to solar energy. He reminded citizens that all government buildings already run on solar power.

The current plan takes inspiration from the Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali Mission, under which more than 12,000 government installations in Bihar have been equipped with solar plants. Building on that momentum, the government now wants to install panels across all domestic buildings within three years.

Why This Matters for Bihar’s Future

This initiative means much more than free panels. It signals a shift in Bihar’s energy story—from dependence on traditional sources to a future powered by sustainability. Families will see lower electricity costs, while the state contributes to India’s clean energy goals.

For millions, sunlight will no longer just brighten homes. It will also power aspirations, reduce expenses, and improve quality of life.

Article Title: Bihar Govt & IIT Delhi Launch AI Training for Engineers in Bridge Design and Monitoring
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
When was the last time you looked at a bridge and thought about the science behind its strength? Starting this September 2025, Bihar is rewriting that story by bringing artificial intelligence, drones, and real-time data into the world of bridge design and safety. And leading this revolution is IIT Delhi, in collaboration with the Bihar government.

Bihar Engineers Step Into the Future

More than 100 government engineers will undergo a six-month certification programme at IIT Delhi. The training will teach them to use AI-driven tools, drones, and sensors for bridge monitoring, design, and maintenance.

This initiative falls under the Bihar State Bridge Management and Maintenance Policy, 2025. Unlike earlier systems, the policy now makes drone-based inspections mandatory for all state-maintained bridges. The shift aims to ensure accuracy, speed, and cost-effectiveness in infrastructure safety.

What Will Engineers Learn?

The new curriculum is not just about theory. It focuses on hands-on technology. Some of the modules include:

AI & Machine Learning: Computing Bridge Health Index (BHI) scores from drone and sensor data. Real-Time Monitoring: Using strain gauges and tilt meters to detect stress points instantly. Smart Planning: Applying Maintenance Priority Index (MPI) models to decide which bridges need urgent repairs.

AI & Machine Learning: Computing Bridge Health Index (BHI) scores from drone and sensor data.

Real-Time Monitoring: Using strain gauges and tilt meters to detect stress points instantly.

Smart Planning: Applying Maintenance Priority Index (MPI) models to decide which bridges need urgent repairs.

These modules promise to make Bihar engineers self-reliant and skilled in future-ready bridge technology.

A Dedicated Bridge Design Cell

Alongside training, the government will set up a Bridge Design Cell under Bihar Rajya Pul Nirman Nigam Limited (BRPNNL). This in-house facility will design bridges, culverts, and retaining walls for Bihar.

Officials estimate that this single step could save over ₹65 crore annually by reducing reliance on external consultants. It also means fewer project delays and faster delivery of safe infrastructure to the public.

Expanding Technical Partnerships

The Bihar government is also in talks with the Indian Academy of Highway Engineers (IAHE) to introduce additional specialized training. Together, these collaborations aim to build a pool of highly skilled bridge engineers who can lead projects not only in Bihar but across India.

Policy That Brings Change

Under the Bihar State Bridge Management and Maintenance Policy, 2025, drone inspections are now compulsory. This approach will help prioritize repairs with real-time accuracy and reduce risks caused by weak structures.

Bihar’s Public Works Minister Nitin Nabin emphasized, “The future of infrastructure lies in technology and self-reliance.” His statement underlines Bihar’s commitment to both innovation and safety.

Rollout Plan for 2025-26

Deployment begins in the financial year 2025-26. In the first phase, 85 bridges will undergo real-time monitoring. Both IIT Delhi and IIT Patna will jointly audit these bridges.

With this move, Bihar isn’t just maintaining old structures. It is building a resilient, tech-powered, and safer bridge network for its people.

Stretching between Auta (Mokama) and Simaria (Begusarai), the six-lane bridge is an engineering feat. With a deck width of 34 meters, it is the widest six-lane bridge in India. For context, most six-lane bridges measure 29.5 meters.

Built at a cost of ₹1,871 crore, the bridge is 8.15 km long, with 1.86 km spanning the Ganga itself. Designed with advanced expansion cable technology, it allows a much smoother flow of vehicles, reducing congestion.

Most importantly, it shortens the distance between North and South Bihar by 100 km, while also easing travel to West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Assam.

Why the Bridge Matters for People

This bridge is more than concrete and steel—it is a lifeline for daily commuters, traders, and families. With faster routes and less congestion, travel time reduces, logistics become cheaper, and opportunities expand.

The project also introduces a Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM), where 60% of the cost is borne by the construction agency and 40% by the government. Later, costs are recovered through tolls. This model is paving the way for future projects in Bihar.

The Buddha Circuit Train: Connecting Heritage and Tourism

Alongside modern infrastructure, Bihar is also reconnecting with its ancient past. A new Buddha Circuit train will link iconic Buddhist sites across Bihar and Jharkhand.

The route begins at Vaishali and covers Hajipur, Patna, Nalanda, Rajgir, Gaya, and Koderma, ensuring seamless travel for pilgrims, tourists, and students.

By bringing sacred sites closer, this train strengthens heritage tourism and reaffirms Bihar’s place as the global center of Buddhist culture.

Bihar’s Expanding Bridge Network

In 2005, Bihar had just four major bridges across the Ganga. Today, the state counts 14 new bridges, with nine more under construction. From JP Setu in Patna to the upcoming Kacchi Dargah–Bidupur bridge, every structure adds to a stronger, better-connected Bihar.

These aren’t just bridges—they are pathways to opportunity, trade, and growth.

Why This Transformation Stands Out

With shorter routes, faster travel, and renewed heritage connections, Bihar is stepping into a new era. The six-lane bridge and Buddha Circuit train are not just projects—they are milestones that carry the hopes of millions.

Why LR Potatoes Are in High Demand

Lady Rosetta (LR) potatoes are widely used for chips, French fries, and snacks. They have qualities that make them the top choice for chips companies:

Round, medium-sized shape perfect for chips machines. Chips absorb less oil and taste crispier. Long shelf life, making storage easier.

Long shelf life, making storage easier.

The government has selected 17 districts for LR potato cultivation: Aurangabad, Banka, Begusarai, Bhagalpur, Gaya, Gopalganj, Katihar, Khagaria, Lakhisarai, Nalanda, Nawada, Patna, Samastipur, Saran, Sheikhpura, Siwan, and Vaishali.

The ideal sowing period is from late October to mid-November. Each hectare needs about 30 quintals of seed, priced at ₹4000 per quintal. With the 75% subsidy, farmers pay much less.

Article Title: Adani Power to Build 2,400 MW Thermal Power Plant in Bihar
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Bihar is gearing up for a historic leap in its energy sector. Adani Power Ltd has secured a Letter of Award (LoA) from the Bihar State Power Generation Company Ltd (BSPGCL) to establish a 2,400 MW greenfield ultra-supercritical thermal power plant in Pirpainti, Bhagalpur district. This project will not only supply electricity but also create jobs, boost industries, and power Bihar’s future growth.

A 25-Year Deal to Light Up Bihar

The LoA confirms a 25-year electricity supply agreement between Adani Power and BSPGCL. Both North Bihar Power Distribution Company Ltd (NBPDCL) and South Bihar Power Distribution Company Ltd (SBPDCL) will benefit from the project.

The plant will have three 800 MW units, designed with ultra-supercritical technology to deliver efficient and reliable electricity.

“With our Pirpainti project in Bihar, we are setting new benchmarks in efficiency and sustainability. This plant will bring affordable and uninterrupted power to the people of Bihar, driving industrialization and prosperity,” said S.B. Khyalia, CEO of Adani Power.

A $3 Billion Investment and Thousands of Jobs

Adani Power plans to invest nearly $3 billion in the plant and related infrastructure. This makes it one of the largest private energy investments in Bihar.

The project will create 10,000–12,000 direct and indirect jobs during construction. Once the plant begins operations, it will continue to employ over 3,000 people, providing stable employment for local communities.

Why Bihar Needs This Energy Boost

India’s electricity demand is rising rapidly. From the current 250 GW, peak demand is projected to touch 400 GW by 2031-32 and exceed 700 GW by 2047. Bihar requires a strong and consistent power supply to support industries, cities, and villages alike.

Although renewable energy is growing, thermal power still ensures round-the-clock reliability. It remains the backbone of India’s energy security, offering crucial base-load and grid balancing support. To meet demand, the government plans to add 100 GW of new thermal capacity by 2035. The Pirpainti project positions Bihar as a central part of this growth strategy.

Article Title: Bihar's First Mushroom Village to Come Up in Nalanda

Article Title: How Engineer Prabhat Kumar Helped 25,000 Farmers Earn Double with SumArth
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
“Never become a farmer.”This was the only advice Prabhat Kumar ever received from his father, a farmer from Gaya, Bihar.

Years later, that very advice inspired him to change the destiny of thousands of farmers. Today, through his initiative SumArth, Prabhat has transformed farming across 500 villages in six districts of Bihar, helping 25,000 farmers double their income by cultivating onions, mushrooms, corn, and strawberries.

Leaving a Global Career to Uplift Bihar with SumArth

Prabhat pursued engineering and co-founded a healthcare company, travelling to 25 countries in the process. Despite his achievements, people mocked his Bihari roots. Many expected him to leave Bihar, just like most professionals.

However, he made a different choice. In 2015, he returned to Gaya and launched SumArth, determined to rewrite Bihar’s farming story. By reconnecting with his roots, he aimed to help the local community achieve prosperity.

Breaking Myths Around Bihar’s Soil with SumArth

Farmers in Gaya often believed the kewal (black) soil could only support paddy and wheat. Moreover, they depended heavily on dealers for seeds and middlemen for sales, earning less than ₹10,000 per acre annually.

Recognizing this gap, Prabhat encouraged farmers to try horticulture crops. He even sent 10 farmers to Maharashtra to witness advanced farming techniques firsthand. There, they discovered a single farmer earning ₹15 lakh from one acre. That eye-opening experience sparked hope and ambition in them.

The Onion Revolution Led by SumArth

The first crop Prabhat introduced was onions. Farmers dedicated 10% of their land to this initiative. Meanwhile, he supported them in building low-cost ventilated storage facilities.

As a result, farmers invested ₹4 per kg and sold at ₹10 per kg, earning ₹1 lakh per acre. Storage facilities allowed them to sell when prices were high, demonstrating that farming could indeed be profitable.

Mushrooms: Turning Costs into Daily Income with SumArth

After onions, mushroom cultivation was introduced to use storage units during winters. Unlike conventional crops, mushrooms required a one-time investment while yielding daily returns.

Consequently, by 2017, 200 farmers joined mushroom farming. Today, 2,000 farmers produce 600 kg of mushrooms daily, while 5,000 continue to benefit from onions. By diversifying crops, Prabhat created multiple income streams for farmers.

Scaling with Corn, Strawberries & Processing Units under SumArth

Encouraged by early successes, farmers explored seed corn, baby corn, and strawberries. In 2023, Prabhat established Gaya’s largest processing unit with a 10,000 kg per day capacity. This extended crop shelf life from 24 hours to 24 months, ensuring farmers could reach larger markets and earn better profits.

Building a Holistic Farming Model with SumArth

SumArth goes beyond crop cultivation. The initiative provides:

Fair-priced inputs for seeds and fertilisers Training on seed treatment and modern crops Awareness programs to prevent fungal attacks Direct marketplaces that eliminate middlemen

Fair-priced inputs for seeds and fertilisers

Training on seed treatment and modern crops

Awareness programs to prevent fungal attacks

Direct marketplaces that eliminate middlemen

As a result, farmers collectively generated ₹100 crore over the last decade. In 2024 alone, their income reached ₹23 crore, proving that a holistic approach could transform rural economies.

What Lies Ahead for SumArth and Bihar Farmers

From 10 farmers in 2015 to 25,000 farmers today, Prabhat’s vision continues to create change. Looking forward, he plans to help farmers increase income fivefold through value-added products.

Meanwhile, SumArth keeps innovating and expanding, giving Bihar’s farmers tools, knowledge, and markets they never had before.

Article Title: Bihar Women Commission launches Online Complaint Filing from 19th September
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
When justice knocks on your door instead of you knocking on its gate, change feels real. Bihar Women Commission has taken such a bold step. Starting 19th September, women across Bihar can register their complaints online without traveling to Patna.

This initiative, launched on the 24th Foundation Day of the Commission, is a historic stride toward making justice faster, fairer, and more accessible.

A Digital Lifeline for Women in Bihar

Till now, women had to reach the Commission office in Patna to file complaints. For those from remote villages, the journey often meant financial stress and emotional struggle.

Now, with the new online process, this hardship ends. Women can simply visit the official website, fill in a digital form, and submit their grievance. This not only saves time and money but also ensures that no woman feels left behind.

How Will the Online Complaint Process Work?

The Commission Chairperson, Apsara Mishra, explained the process clearly. The system is designed to be as easy as filling out a student admission form online.

Women need to enter their name, address, mobile number, and case details. They must provide the details of the person against whom they are filing. A separate column lets them select the complaint category—domestic violence, dowry harassment, sexual harassment, property dispute, or others.

Women need to enter their name, address, mobile number, and case details.

They must provide the details of the person against whom they are filing.

A separate column lets them select the complaint category—domestic violence, dowry harassment, sexual harassment, property dispute, or others.

Finally, the woman can complete the process with a digital signature. This ensures authenticity and prevents fake or incomplete submissions.

Faster Action, Transparent Monitoring

The moment a complaint is filed online, the technical cell and relevant officers get notified. After a preliminary review, the complainant receives updates about the next steps.

Moreover, the digital process allows the Commission to maintain a record of every case. This enhances transparency, helps in monitoring, and ensures better follow-up.

With this, women no longer have to spend days traveling or waiting. Instead, their concerns get attention more quickly and efficiently.

Why This Change Matters Now

For years, women from distant districts faced difficulty reaching Patna. Some never came forward due to cost, time, or hesitation. This digital leap removes those barriers.

It also aligns with the Digital India mission, making governance inclusive and tech-driven. Importantly, it shows that Bihar is ready to empower women with practical solutions, not just promises.

A Step Dedicated to Women’s Dignity

Chairperson Apsara Mishra stated, “Many women hesitated to travel far and narrate their pain. Now, they can raise their voice from home. Our goal is that no woman should wander for justice.”

This reflects a deep commitment to accessibility and dignity. Justice, after all, should not be a privilege—it must be a right that reaches every doorstep.

Article Title: Gaya Ji Pitru Paksha Fair 2025: Vishnupad Declared No Pollution, No Horn, No Vehicle Zone
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Bihar’s Sacred Fair Gets a Pollution-Free Makeover

Every year, lakhs of pilgrims from across India and abroad gather in Gaya Ji to honor their ancestors during the Pitru Paksha Mela. This year, the district administration has taken a remarkable step to ensure comfort, safety, and spirituality blend together.

The Vishnupad temple area has been officially declared a No Pollution, No Horn, and No Vehicle Zone. This initiative aims to provide a peaceful atmosphere to devotees while keeping the sacred site clean and congestion-free.

The Big Step Towards a Hassle-Free Pilgrimage

To implement this change, DM Shashank Shubhankar and SSP Anand Kumar personally traveled by e-rickshaw from Chand Choura to Vishnupad Mandir, symbolizing the new system. By doing this, they not only set an example but also encouraged devotees to embrace this eco-friendly approach.

Importantly, vehicles are now restricted beyond Chand Choura and Bengali Ashram. Pilgrims can only reach the temple either by foot or through free e-rickshaw services provided by the administration. This move ensures the narrow temple lanes remain free from traffic jams, making the spiritual journey smooth and serene.

Special Facilities for Devotees and Seniors

Understanding the needs of elderly visitors, the administration has deployed 60 e-rickshaws in three shifts. From Pretshila parking points to Pretshila temple, special arrangements have been made so that senior citizens face no difficulty.

Additionally, at Gaya Railway Station, pilgrims will find free e-rickshaw services to different pind-daan spots. This facility will not only save time but also offer much-needed convenience for those unfamiliar with the city.

Why This Step Matters for Bihar and Pilgrims

The Pitru Paksha Mela is not just a religious gathering; it is a lifeline of Bihar’s cultural and spiritual identity. With lakhs of devotees pouring in, mismanagement can lead to chaos. However, this eco-conscious decision brings hope that the Vishnupad temple complex will remain safe, pollution-free, and spiritually uplifting.

Moreover, this effort reflects how Bihar is gradually embracing modern solutions while respecting deep-rooted traditions.

Article Title: No coach, no fancy gear: Bihar labourer finishes as runner-up in Spiti marathon
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A Runner With No Coach, No Gear—Just Grit

“No coach. No fancy gear. Just raw resolve.” That’s how the Army described Rohit Kumar, a 32-year-old daily wage labourer from Khagaria, Bihar, who recently stunned the nation with his marathon achievement.

Working at a construction site in Delhi, Rohit spends his mornings not on rest but on the road. While most wake up at sunrise, he laces his worn-out shoes at 4:30 am. His dream? To one day wear the Indian jersey at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics in the Triathlon.

Spiti Marathon Glory Against All Odds

At the Surya Spiti Challenge 2025, Rohit competed in the brutal 77 km Kunzum La–Kaza Ultra. With icy winds, thin air, and steep climbs, this race isn’t for the faint-hearted. Yet Rohit crossed the finish line second, clocking 7 hours and 44 minutes.

The Army’s Uttar Bharat shared his story on X, writing:“He doesn’t chase records or sponsorships. He runs to survive. His finish line was not just a medal—it was dignity, hope, and a step closer to his Olympic dream.”

This wasn’t his first big achievement. In fact, Rohit has participated in more than 100 marathons, often averaging five races in a single month. Now, he says he focuses on quality over quantity.

Life Between Labour and Long Runs

Balancing life as a construction worker with the demands of training isn’t easy. Yet Rohit chooses sacrifice over excuses. Out of his modest ₹30,000 monthly income, he spends nearly ₹20,000 on his diet and running equipment.

Inspired by marathon greats from London, New York, and Tokyo, he began training in 2020 without a coach. Every run is self-taught, every step powered by sheer will. And when asked about his next step, he simply smiles: “I will get another podium finish.”

The Road Ahead: Arunachal and Beyond

After Spiti, Rohit has already received an invitation to another high-altitude marathon in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh. The Indian Army has promised to take care of his travel, food, and lodging. He hopes this will be another podium finish that pushes him closer to his Olympic dream.

For Rohit, the journey is about more than medals. He runs for those who remain unseen—the countless daily wage workers who shoulder heavy burdens yet carry silent dreams in their hearts.

Article Title: Bihar Idea Festival 2025: 25,000 Startup Ideas and BIIPP 2025 Put Bihar on India’s Industrial Map
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A Wave of Ideas from the Heart of Bihar

What happens when a state unlocks the entrepreneurial spirit of its youth? Bihar just answered that with the Bihar Idea Festival 2025, where an astounding 25,000 startup ideas poured in from every district. The finale, held at Bapu Sabhagar, Patna, was not just a celebration of ideas but also a showcase of Bihar’s bold leap into industrial growth, global exports, and inclusive entrepreneurship.

Big Announcements That Redefine Bihar’s Future

The event concluded with the launch of Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Package (BIIPP) 2025, the One Block One Product (OBOP) initiative, and the opening of the APEDA regional office in Patna. Together, these moves position Bihar as a rising hub for investment, industry, and export.

Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal praised Bihar’s new policies and called BIIPP 2025 one of the most liberal packages in India. With incentives such as free land, 300% SGST reimbursement, and strong startup support, Bihar is clearly preparing for a transformational journey. He also announced the Centre’s approval of four new industrial parks and reaffirmed plans for the 3,000-acre industrial township in Gaya.

A Changed Bihar: From Small Budgets to Big Dreams

Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary highlighted the state’s progress. Bihar’s budget once stood at ₹6,000 crore. Today, it has risen to ₹37,000 crore, fueling jobs and industrial growth. He urged the Centre to consider new industrial corridors to meet the aspirations of Bihar’s 14 crore population.

M. Kumar Singh, Additional Chief Secretary of the Industries Department, shared key details of BIIPP 2025. Job-creating industries can now access up to 25 acres of free land, while others get 50% concession on BIADA land rates. Add to that capital subsidies, export promotion incentives, and green industry support—and Bihar’s industrial ecosystem suddenly looks more attractive than ever.

One Block One Product: Taking Bihar’s Treasures to the World

The OBOP initiative is extending the successful ODOP model to all 534 blocks. From Bhagalpur silk to Muzaffarpur’s Shahi litchi, from Darbhanga makhana to Madhubani paintings, each block will now receive branding, packaging, certification, and global market access.

The Chief Minister Entrepreneur Scheme and Bihar Micro Entrepreneur Scheme were also highlighted, which have already supported more than 43,500 entrepreneurs—many scaling their businesses beyond ₹1 crore turnover.

25,000 Ideas, 5 Winning Innovations

Shradha Sharma, Founder & CEO of YourStory, who spearheaded the outreach, shared how the festival exceeded expectations. “We set out to collect 10,000 ideas. Bihar’s youth gave us 25,000, even from schoolchildren in Classes 9 and 10. This shows Bihar’s hidden entrepreneurial energy,” she said.

Industries Minister Nitish Mishra underlined Bihar’s readiness to become a serious player in India’s industrial map. From special economic zones to land banks, and from OBOP support to startup funding, Bihar is creating a full-fledged growth ecosystem.

Article Title: Bihar govt makes Student Credit Card loans interest-free
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Patna, Bihar: Imagine studying without worrying about loan interest piling up. For thousands of students in Bihar, that dream is now a reality.

The Bihar government has announced that all Student Credit Card (SCC) loans under the Saat Nischay Yojana are now completely interest-free. This step is designed to reduce financial stress for students and give them the freedom to focus entirely on their education.

What’s New in the Student Credit Card Scheme?

Earlier, education loans carried interest—4% for general students, and a reduced 1% for female, differently-abled, and transgender students. Now, every student will pay zero interest.

Repayment terms have also been made easier:

Loans up to ₹2 lakh: Repayment period extended from 5 years to 7 years. Loans above ₹2 lakh: Repayment period extended from 7 years to 10 years.

Loans up to ₹2 lakh: Repayment period extended from 5 years to 7 years.

Loans above ₹2 lakh: Repayment period extended from 7 years to 10 years.

This means students can pay back in smaller installments over a longer time, easing financial pressure.

Why This Change Matters for Students

The rising cost of higher education often stops students from pursuing their dreams. By removing interest and giving more time to repay, Bihar is helping young learners continue their studies without fear of debt.

The SCC scheme already allowed loans of up to ₹4 lakh for higher education. With the new update, it is now even more accessible and supportive for students from every background.

A Step Toward Accessible Education

This move is more than a policy—it’s a message that education should not come with financial barriers. Students now have the freedom to choose courses and colleges with confidence. They can focus on learning, gaining skills, and building careers, instead of worrying about repayment stress.

In the long run, this support can open doors for more engineers, doctors, researchers, and professionals from Bihar, shaping a brighter future for the state and its youth.

The Road Ahead for Bihar’s Students

Interest-free loans and flexible repayment terms will inspire many more students to step into higher education. It means better opportunities, more graduates, and stronger representation of Bihar’s talent in India and beyond.

Article Title: Purnia Gets Airport, Expressway, and Vande Bharat Boost
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
From Bullock Carts to Vande Bharat: Purnia’s Remarkable Journey of Airports, Expressways, and Dreams Taking Flight

Purnia: From Forgotten Dusty Trails to the Sky

Once upon a time, Purnia was a district marked by dusty paths, bullock carts, and grinding poverty. Writer Phanishwar Nath Renu, in classics like Maila Anchal and Mare Gaye Gulfaam, painted this picture of despair. But today, that same Purnia is rewriting its destiny. From airports to expressways and the Vande Bharat Train, this district is stepping into a new era of growth.

The First-Ever Patna–Purnia Expressway

Connectivity fuels progress, and Purnia has finally received its most ambitious road project—the Patna-Purnia Expressway. Recently declared National Expressway-9 (NE-9) by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, this will be Bihar’s first expressway built entirely within state borders. As a result, travel between Patna and Purnia will become smoother, faster, and more reliable. Businesses, education, and healthcare will expand as better roads create stronger bridges to opportunity.

Purnia Airport: A New Gateway to the World

On Monday, PM Narendra Modi inaugurated the new terminal building at Purnia Airport, making it Bihar’s fourth operational commercial airport after Patna, Gaya, and Darbhanga. For the first time, people here can take off directly to major cities. In fact, nearly two crore residents of Seemanchal, Kosi, Bhagalpur, West Bengal, and even Nepal will benefit.

Now, reaching Kolkata will take just 70 minutes. Ahmedabad will be within two hours, and Delhi much quicker than ever before. This isn’t just about travel—it’s about opening doors to education, healthcare, trade, and agriculture markets that once seemed far away.

Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat Trains: Speed on Rails

Railways are no longer just about distance; they’re about dignity and dreams. Rajesh Ranjan (Pappu Yadav) flagged off both Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat Trains from Purnia Junction, celebrating decades of public struggle and aspiration. For the people of Seemanchal and Kosi, these trains symbolize more than transport. They represent confidence, mobility, and the power to connect with India’s fastest-growing hubs.

Purnia’s Transformation in Just 20 Years

In only two decades, Purnia has flipped its narrative. Where once poverty dictated lives, now development inspires futures. Expressways, airports, and modern trains are no longer distant promises—they are here. And more projects are already lined up to add to this momentum.

People who once relied on bullock carts are now boarding flights. Villagers who once traveled days for healthcare or jobs can now reach metros in hours. Purnia isn’t just changing—it’s shining.

A New Dawn for Bhagalpur’s Vikramshila

History and higher education are coming together in Bhagalpur, where land acquisition has begun for the proposed Vikramshila Central University. The new campus will rise near the Vikramshila excavation site, one of Bihar’s most significant cultural and archaeological treasures.

With survey work already underway, this development is being seen as a turning point for both the region’s academic aspirations and its historic pride.

Land Acquisition and Survey Work Underway

The Land Acquisition Department has started publishing the list of landholders. Authorities have earmarked around 215 acres of land for the project.

84 acres in Malakpur

Much of this land is currently agricultural, featuring lush mango orchards. Some huts stand on government land, but most of the plots remain suitable for institutional use.

Officials confirmed that survey work is proceeding under Section 19(1) of the Land Acquisition Act. After publishing the list of landholders, a 60-day claim and objection period will follow. Subsequently, valuation notices will be issued, and payments will be made to eligible landowners.

A Committee to Decide Land Value

To ensure fairness, the Education Department has already proposed acquiring 4.29 acres close to the excavation site. A six-member committee will soon be formed to determine the land’s value.

The establishment of Vikramshila Central University will do more than just create another academic hub. It will reconnect modern Bihar with its ancient legacy of learning, once nurtured by the Vikramshila Mahavihara.

Article Title: Bihar Government’s Agriculture Department Wins Scotch Gold Award

Bihar Government Wins Scotch Gold Award: A Historic Achievement

Bihar’s Agriculture Department has recently received the prestigious Scotch Gold Award, recognizing excellence in agriculture and innovative initiatives. This award celebrates the department’s consistent efforts to enhance farmer welfare, promote sustainable practices, and implement impactful programs. Moreover, it positions Bihar as a state leading in agricultural development and environmental responsibility.

Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary: Bihar’s Ecological Treasure

Located in Bhagalpur, the Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary is India’s only dolphin sanctuary. Spanning nearly 60 kilometers of the Ganga River, it is home to the endangered Gangetic dolphin, India’s national aquatic mammal. The sanctuary plays a crucial role in conserving this vulnerable species while safeguarding the broader river ecosystem.

Furthermore, it attracts researchers, environmentalists, and eco-tourists who wish to witness the rare aquatic wildlife and understand river ecology first-hand.

Conservation Efforts and Biodiversity

The sanctuary is not limited to dolphins. It hosts smooth-coated otters, freshwater turtles, and a variety of waterbirds. Conservation teams, alongside local communities, work tirelessly to prevent river pollution, illegal fishing, and other threats. They actively monitor wildlife, educate locals, and implement sustainable practices that ensure the long-term survival of these species.

Consequently, the sanctuary is becoming a model for community-led environmental conservation, proving that human intervention can harmonize with nature.

Bihar on the Global Environmental Map

Through initiatives like the Vikramshila Dolphin Sanctuary, Bihar is gaining global recognition for its environmental stewardship. The sanctuary highlights the state’s commitment to protecting endangered species while promoting eco-tourism and raising awareness about biodiversity. It reflects a balance between ecological preservation and socio-economic development, making Bihar a model for other regions.

Article Title: Bihar’s Pakauli Village Where Every Home Blooms With Sandalwood for Every Daughter’s Birth
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
The Enchanting Sandalwood Tradition of Pakauli

In Bihar’s Pakauli village, a unique aroma welcomes visitors—sandalwood wafts from almost every home. Nestled about 35 km from Patna in Vaishali district, this village celebrates the birth of daughters with more than just joy. Families plant sandalwood trees as a mark of happiness and prosperity.

With nearly 700 houses and a population around 4,000, Pakauli now boasts over 900 sandalwood trees. As you stroll through the village, every doorway reveals this fragrant tradition.

A Tradition Rooted in Celebration

Unlike many parts of Bihar, where sandalwood struggles to grow, Pakauli has made it thrive. Locals say whenever a daughter is born, a sandalwood tree is planted. While the exact origins of this tradition remain unclear, villagers confirm it has been followed for generations.

Over time, the trees have become more than symbols—they embody blessings, protection, and family pride.

The Magic of Malagiri Sandalwood

Pakauli grows Malagiri sandalwood, famed for its soft, captivating fragrance that lasts long. Its uses range from religious rituals to skin care products. Families especially cherish it during poojas, tilak ceremonies, and festivals.

Villagers describe the aroma as almost mystical, filling the air around homes and connecting the community through scent and celebration.

Nature’s Own Miracle

The process feels magical. Birds often drop sandalwood seeds in the fields. Over time, these seeds sprout into young trees, later transplanted in front of homes. Families say the trees act like a family member, sharing every joy and sorrow.

It is common to see these trees standing tall outside every house, creating a serene and sacred atmosphere.

Valuing the Sacred Trees

Sandalwood isn’t just symbolic—it’s valuable. Young saplings cost around ₹100, while mature trees can fetch between ₹50,000 and ₹2 lakh, attracting buyers even from Haryana. The trees take 10–12 years to reach full size, making them both a cherished asset and a source of income.

Local people also believe sandalwood is auspicious. It plays a role in weddings, rituals, and even funerals, making it central to cultural and economic life in Pakauli.

A Fragrant Gift for Daughters

Pakauli’s unique tradition ensures every daughter is celebrated with enduring symbolism. As the trees grow alongside them, the fragrance of sandalwood becomes a living testimony to love, prosperity, and continuity.

This village shows how traditions, culture, and nature can intertwine beautifully, preserving values while contributing to livelihoods.

Article Title: Patna’s Ganga River to get its first Water Metro this Dussehra
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
This Dussehra, Patna is set to surprise its people with a stunning electric water metro — a game-changer for travel on the Ganga.

A New Era of Travel on the Ganga

Patna’s Ganga riverfront is entering a new chapter. The sleek electric vessel MV-Gomdhar Kunwar has finally arrived in the city, bringing the long-awaited water metro service closer than ever.

The project is a joint effort between the Bihar Tourism Department and the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI). Built in Kolkata by Hooghly Cochin Shipyard Limited at a cost of nearly ₹12 crore, this ship reflects India’s growing capability in modern water transport.

Digha to Kangan Ghat: The First Route

The water metro will start by running between Digha Ghat and Kangan Ghat, covering a stretch of 6.5 km. In addition, plans include extending the service to Gandhi Ghat, which would make the route 9.5 km long.

With 50 cushioned seats and standing space for 25 passengers, the air-conditioned boat promises both comfort and safety. Moreover, large glass windows will allow travelers to capture breathtaking views of the Ganga while seated indoors.

Designed for Comfort and Technology

This ship is more than just a vessel. In fact, it offers a unique river cruise experience.

Four air-conditioners ensure comfort even in hot weather. CCTV cameras, LCD screens, and sound systems provide safety and real-time updates. Wide glass panels let passengers enjoy uninterrupted river views.

Four air-conditioners ensure comfort even in hot weather.

CCTV cameras, LCD screens, and sound systems provide safety and real-time updates.

Wide glass panels let passengers enjoy uninterrupted river views.

Therefore, every ride will feel like a scenic journey rather than a daily commute.

Eco-Friendly and Affordable

The MV-Gomdhar Kunwar also marks a move toward sustainable urban mobility. Since it runs on batteries, the impact on the river’s ecosystem remains minimal.

The batteries charge within half an hour and power the ship for about 90 minutes. Charging points are already installed at Gaighat and Digha jetties.

Equally important, the fare will remain affordable. Authorities expect it to range between ₹20 and ₹30 per kilometer per person, making it accessible to both daily commuters and tourists.

The Journey from Kolkata to Patna

The ship began its journey from Kolkata on September 9 and reached Patna on September 27. Strong winds and high water levels delayed its arrival. However, it safely reached Gaighat port, where IWAI officials Arvind Kumar and Amit Kumar welcomed it.

Now, final technical checks are underway. Once cleared, the ship will be handed over to the Bihar State Tourism Development Corporation (BSTDC) for operation. Most likely, its official launch will happen during Dussehra.

Experience Ganga Like Never Before

Imagine sitting inside a cool, air-conditioned hall with glass windows all around, while the mighty Ganga flows beside you. That is the experience Patna’s new water metro promises.

This is not just about transport. Instead, it is about reclaiming the river as a space for both travel and tourism. With this step, Bihar is adding a new dimension to its urban lifestyle while also inviting the world to see the state differently.

Organized by the Department of Radiation Oncology, the event celebrated Breast Cancer Awareness Month, reminding everyone that early detection can save lives.

A Walk for Hope and Health

To make the message resonate deeply, BSc Nursing students performed a nukkad natak (street play) at the OPD Foyer. Through drama and emotion, they explained the importance of early detection, regular screening, and self-examination.

Article Title: Top 5 Crops That Make Bihar an ‘Agri Powerhouse’ Beyond Makhana and Litchi
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Bihar’s Fields Tell a Bigger Story

When you think of Bihar, two names usually come up — Makhana and Litchi.However, the state’s story doesn’t stop there. Over the years, Bihar has emerged as one of India’s most dynamic agricultural powerhouses. Its farmers are now combining traditional knowledge with modern farming techniques, transforming the state into a leader across multiple crops.

Let’s take a closer look at the five crops that make Bihar the pride of Indian agriculture.

1. Litchi — The Royal Fruit with Global Appeal

The world knows Bihar for its Shahi Litchi, a fruit so special that it carries a Geographical Indication (GI) tag. Every year, the state produces 3 to 3.22 lakh tonnes, contributing nearly 43% of India’s total litchi output.

Moreover, Bihar’s litchi isn’t confined to Indian markets. It travels to the UK, UAE, Nepal, France, and Australia, earning foreign exchange and fame for local farmers. Thanks to its flavor and freshness, the “Shahi Litchi” has become Bihar’s sweet ambassador across continents.

2. Makhana — The White Gold of Mithila

Next comes Mithila Makhana, another gem that carries a GI tag and deep cultural roots. Bihar contributes 80–90% of India’s total makhana production. The state annually produces around 10,000–1,20,000 tonnes of seeds and nearly 40,000 tonnes of processed makhana.

Beyond domestic markets, Mithila’s Makhana is exported to the USA, UAE, Canada, and Australia. Farmers call it “white gold” — a symbol of pride and prosperity. Over time, it has also turned into one of India’s fastest-growing superfoods, loved for its nutrition and crunch.

3. Mushroom — The New Face of Bihar’s Farming

In recent years, Bihar has turned its attention to mushroom cultivation — and the results are impressive. Since 2021, mushroom production has grown rapidly, positioning Bihar among India’s top producers.

Every year, the state produces around 28,000–41,000 tonnes, accounting for 10–12% of India’s total yield. Farmers primarily grow Button and Oyster mushrooms, using low-cost sheds and modern composting methods. As a result, mushrooms from Bihar now reach West Bengal, Jharkhand, and even countries like Japan and Nepal.

Clearly, Bihar is no longer relying only on traditional crops — it’s experimenting, innovating, and thriving.

4. Singhada (Water Chestnut) — Turning Water into Wealth

Bihar’s wetlands have found a new treasure — Singhada (Water Chestnut). The state produces 50,000–1,00,000 tonnes annually, and about 80% of this comes from North Bihar.

Because of its high demand and easy adaptability, Singhada has become a profitable choice for small-scale farmers. The fruit now travels to the US, UK, Canada, Saudi Arabia, and Singapore. With proper packaging and cold-chain facilities, this aquatic crop has turned stagnant ponds into sources of steady income.

5. Bottle Gourd — A Common Crop with Uncommon Impact

The humble Bottle Gourd (Lauki) might not sound glamorous, yet it has immense value. Bihar produces 6.5 to 6.6 lakh tonnes annually, contributing nearly 20% of India’s total yield.

Because of the state’s fertile Gangetic plains, Lauki thrives throughout the summer and monsoon seasons. Most of the production serves local markets, but Bihar also exports to Bangladesh and Nepal. In a health-conscious world, where demand for light, nutritious food is growing, Lauki gives Bihar another strong edge.

Bihar’s Power Beyond the Top Five

The list doesn’t end here. Bihar ranks second in Jute and Mesta production and third in Potato, Lentil, Green Chili, Okra, and Cauliflower. It also ranks fourth in fruits and vegetables such as Mango, Onion, Carrot, and Eggplant, and fifth in Sunflower, Sugarcane, and Maize.

Such variety proves that Bihar is not just sustaining agriculture — it is leading it through diversity.

What Makes Bihar’s Agriculture So Strong?

Several factors have fueled Bihar’s agricultural transformation:

Fertile alluvial soil and rich water resources from the Ganga plains. Government initiatives supporting irrigation, subsidies, and crop diversification. Farmers adopting modern techniques like drip irrigation and organic farming. Expanding export opportunities that link Bihar’s produce to global markets.

Fertile alluvial soil and rich water resources from the Ganga plains.

Government initiatives supporting irrigation, subsidies, and crop diversification.

Farmers adopting modern techniques like drip irrigation and organic farming.

Expanding export opportunities that link Bihar’s produce to global markets.

Furthermore, the shift from traditional methods to smart, scientific farming has boosted both productivity and profitability. Bihar’s farmlands are no longer seen as outdated — they are symbols of innovation and sustainability.

❤️ The Soul of Bihar’s Soil

Once labeled as a backward state, Bihar is now scripting a remarkable turnaround through agriculture. From Shahi Litchi to Mithila Makhana, and from Mushrooms to Singhada, every crop carries the essence of Bihar’s determination and progress.

ECI Declares Paid Holiday for All Bihar Employees on Polling Days — Empowering Every Voter

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has taken a strong step to boost voter turnout in Bihar. It has announced that all employees in the state, including daily and casual workers, will get a paid holiday on polling days during the upcoming General Assembly elections and bye-elections across eight constituencies.

This proactive move aims to remove one of the biggest hurdles in voting — work commitments — and ensure that every eligible citizen gets the time and freedom to vote.

The decision comes under Section 135B of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, which legally requires employers to grant a paid holiday to every employee who is entitled to vote.

If an employer denies this right or deducts wages for the day, strict action can follow. The ECI’s clear message is simple — voting is not just a right, it’s a protected duty.

Imagine a future where your home state becomes a tech-hub, where chips, AI labs and high-end manufacturing don’t just lie in the big metros—but bloom right here. That’s exactly what Bihar’s announcement signals. On 28 October 2025, CM Nitish Kumar declared that Bihar will host clusters for artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor manufacturing—mirroring the ambitions of states like Odisha, Karnataka and Gujarat. This isn’t just another statement. It marks a turning point, especially for a generation that has watched so many migrate for opportunity.

Why This Matters

Industrial leap

By launching AI and semiconductor clusters, Bihar takes a bold step into high-tech manufacturing. As the announcement explains, the state will tie up with the Centre’s “India Semiconductor Mission” for chip manufacturing, packaging and design units. Such industries require clean power, efficient water, skilled labour—all elements the CM claims Bihar now possesses. Thus, Bihar shifts from being perceived only as a labour-supplier to becoming a manufacturer and innovator.

Massive jobs & livelihoods

Crucially, the plan places job-creation at its heart. High-tech units tend to bring in more than just workers—they demand engineers, designers, technicians, apprentices. That means local youth can stay home and build futures. The article asserts “high-tech employment, investment growth and industrial transformation” will result.

Inviting investments & resources

The announcement emphasises inviting entrepreneurs and investors—especially those from Bihar who have made their mark elsewhere—to bring industries home.Plus, public-sector giants (Maharatna, Navratna companies) will deploy industry units, offering credibility, scale and resource-backing.

The Road Ahead: What Needs to Happen

Infrastructure must match ambition

Even the best plans falter when infrastructure lags. To succeed, these clusters will require reliable power, clean water, good transport, and skilled manpower. The announcement acknowledges as much—”industrial corridors, high-quality power supply, water management and skilled human resources are necessary.” Hence, the state must ensure road-maps are laid out, timelines fixed and accountability visible.

Skill-building & education

A cluster is only as good as its workforce. Bihar already flagged an AI-education initiative for students under CM Nitish earlier this year, showing the direction. Now, bridging school, college and industry must become seamless: so that youth can walk from graduation straight into tech labs, not migrate away.

Sustained policy, not headline promises

Announcements are vital—but execution will define outcomes. The state must maintain favourable policy, ease of doing business, and consistent support across political cycles. In other words: this can’t fade after the headlines.

What It Means for You and Me

If you’re a young person in Bihar, a parent, a local entrepreneur or community member—this is more than news. It can translate into opportunity. You may no longer need to leave Bihar to seek high-end jobs. New workshops, design labs, chip-units might open near you.If you’re an investor or entrepreneur with roots in Bihar: here’s a signal to come home, re-invest talent, resources and ambitions.And for all of us who think of Bihar in traditional terms—it’s time to reimagine. The state is signalling it can be tech-strong, industrially capable, and globally competitive.

Why This Story Should Be Told

Because stories shape perception. Because for too long, Bihar’s narrative has centred on migration, under-employment and opportunity-loss. This is a story of turnaround, of where the young might stay and build their future.That is precisely why we at Bihar Say share it. We believe Bihar’s next story is one of transformation—of tech-hubs, innovation, and rooted talent.

Article Title: Bihar EOU blocks over 20,000 mobile numbers in cybercrime crackdown
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A Digital Tsunami Hits Bihar

The digital storm landed hard in Bihar—and this time, it wasn’t business as usual. The Economic Offences Unit (EOU) has deactivated over 20,000 mobile numbers, blocked more than 13,000 IMEIs, and frozen crores in bank accounts to clamp down on cybercrime. This decisive action shows Bihar is no longer a passive victim—it’s fighting back with precision and purpose.

Inside the Crackdown: The Numbers Tell a Story

From January to September 2025, Bihar logged around 74,000 online fraud complaints. The EOU responded decisively, freezing ₹75.92 crore—just over 21% of reported losses—and returning ₹5.14 crore to victims.

In October alone, 249 mobile numbers linked to online scams were deactivated. The department has also begun a rigorous investigation into “mule accounts,” which are bank accounts used to launder fraudulent money. In August, officials flagged nearly 200 such accounts and retrieved information on 138 of them through national data systems.

Furthermore, over 513 social media posts and profiles spreading misinformation or promoting scams have been removed. Every measure adds another layer of protection for Bihar’s digital citizens.

Why This Crackdown Matters

1. Rising Threats in the Digital Era

Bihar’s growing internet reach has brought new challenges. While access improves lives, it also exposes users to phishing, fake investment schemes, and online job scams. Many victims come from semi-urban and rural backgrounds, where digital literacy remains low.

2. A Statewide Impact

Cybercrime isn’t confined to Patna or urban centers. Small towns and villages have also faced the brunt of fraudsters targeting unsuspecting users. This crackdown sends a clear message—no corner of Bihar is off the radar.

3. Building Digital Trust

The EOU’s ongoing actions reinforce public faith in the system. By tracking transactions, blocking devices, and freezing suspicious accounts, authorities are restoring confidence in online financial activity and digital safety.

Step-by-Step: How the EOU Is Winning the Battle

Mobile number blocking: Over 20,000 SIM cards linked to scams deactivated. IMEI lockdown: More than 13,000 mobile devices rendered unusable. Social media monitoring: Over 500 misleading profiles and posts removed.

Each of these steps pushes Bihar closer to a secure and accountable digital space.

What It Means for Citizens

Every digital user in Bihar plays a role in this transformation. Awareness and caution are now vital weapons. Avoid sharing OTPs, clicking unknown links, or trusting random investment calls. If a message or transaction feels suspicious, report it immediately.

This campaign proves something powerful—when technology is misused, Bihar will act. With the EOU leading from the front, the message is unmistakable: cybercriminals can no longer hide behind screens.

Article Title: Patna Physician Unveils Doxycycline’s STI Prevention Potential at IDWeek, Atlanta
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A Bold Statement from Patna on the Global Health Stage

The moment felt electric: a senior physician from Patna walked into the room in Atlanta and declared that a 70-year-old generic antibiotic might soon shift the dynamics of STI prevention. At IDWeek 2025, a global infectious-disease gathering, he presented emerging evidence that using Doxycycline after sexual exposure—or in some trials before high-risk contact—can sharply cut rates of bacterial STIs like syphilis and chlamydia. According to his summary of international data, reductions of 80% or more are becoming plausible.

In fact, one real-world study found reductions of 86.4% for syphilis and 89.7% for chlamydia when doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (doxy-PEP) was used.

Yet, as the Patna physician emphasised, this is not a silver bullet. He stressed the need for medical supervision, regular STI testing, and antibiotic resistance monitoring. After all, the global agency World Health Organization (WHO) in 2025 explicitly began developing guidelines on doxycycline prophylaxis for STIs.

What the Evidence Shows — And Why It’s Ground-Shifting

Emerging Data.Several studies now support the idea that doxycycline taken within 72 hours of unprotected sex can dramatically reduce certain bacterial STI risks. In one randomized trial among men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women, incidence of syphilis, chlamydia and gonorrhoea dropped significantly. Infectious Diseases Society of America Another real-world dataset supported these findings.

Key Findings:

Reduction in syphilis and chlamydia cases reached up to ~80-90% in some cohorts. Effect on gonorrhoea is more modest and currently under question. The WHO is reviewing and considering formal guideline development for doxycycline prophylaxis in STIs.

Why It Matters.In many countries—including India—the burden of bacterial STIs remains high, yet prevention tools have stagnated. Here, an age-old antibiotic repurposed for prophylaxis could be a game-changer. Moreover, having a physician from Patna bring these results to a major international conference underscores how local expertise is now emerging as global voice.

From Patna to Atlanta: A Spotlight on the Physician’s Role

Diwakar Tejaswi (Senior Physician, Patna) took the stage in Atlanta and framed the data through a global-local lens. He argued that while the trials were conducted in Western countries and among high-risk groups, the findings have relevance for India as well—especially for populations that face educational or access barriers.

Importantly, Dr Tejaswi stressed responsibility:

“While doxycycline shows promise, responsible usage and ongoing research are essential to prevent resistance and ensure patient safety.”

That message resonates particularly in India, where antibiotic misuse remains high and resistance trends are well-documented.

Opportunities for India — With Clear Caution Flags

Potential Pathways:

Indian clinicians could consider doxy-PEP for high-risk individuals under supervised protocols. Public-health authorities might integrate doxycycline prophylaxis into broader STI‐control guidelines if further Indian trials validate efficacy and safety.

Article Title: Patna to Get Multi-Modal Hub, Model Vending Zone & Elevated Road Near Airport
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A City on the Move

Drive through Patna today, and you can feel the pulse of change. The capital of Bihar isn’t standing still anymore—it’s evolving fast. The city is preparing for a major transformation under Chief Minister Nitish Kumar’s Pragati Yatra on February 21, where projects worth nearly ₹1,350 crore will be launched.

Among these initiatives are a multi-modal hub, a model vending zone, and an elevated road near the airport—each one crafted to ease congestion and modernize city life. Together, they mark a turning point for Patna’s urban future.

Multi-Modal Hub: Where All Roads Meet

Patna’s upcoming multi-modal hub will unify the way people move. It’s designed to bring buses, autos, e-rickshaws, and inter-city transport under one modern roof.

The plan includes a multi-level complex near GPO, linked to Patna Junction through a pedestrian subway. It will feature digital displays, elevators, EV charging bays, and spacious waiting zones. Moreover, real-time coordination between transit modes will cut travel time significantly.

This is not just a structure—it’s a statement of intent. As traffic density grows, the hub will simplify commutes, reduce chaos, and create a smoother, greener mobility experience for citizens.

Model Vending Zone: Empowering the Heart of the Market

Patna’s streets have long been a mix of energy and congestion. Street vendors bring life to the city, yet the lack of structured space has caused frequent traffic snarls.

To address this, the administration is developing model vending zones that balance order with opportunity. Vendors will now operate from well-defined stalls with lighting, sanitation, and storage facilities. Additionally, proper footpaths will return to pedestrians, easing both movement and safety.

This initiative celebrates inclusivity. Instead of displacing traders, it integrates them into a cleaner, more organized ecosystem—preserving livelihoods while reshaping urban flow.

Elevated Road Near Airport: A Gateway to Global Patna

The new elevated road near Jay Prakash Narayan Airport is another bold step forward. With passenger traffic rising after the new terminal opening, this link will ensure swift and seamless access.

The project envisions a four-lane elevated corridor that cuts travel time from city centers to the airport dramatically. Furthermore, it connects to broader infrastructure goals under the Patna Ring Road plan, strengthening routes to Bihta and beyond.

For travelers, this means fewer jams and quicker routes. For businesses, it’s a sign that Patna is ready for global attention.

A Ripple Effect Across Rural Patna

While urban projects take the spotlight, rural Patna isn’t left behind. A new road will soon link the Bihta–Sarmera route with Daniyawan Top, improving inter-block travel. Local residents near Naubatpur have also been advocating for a flyover at Nispura Lakh—a long-pending demand that might finally see approval.

Additionally, large ponds and lakes are being rejuvenated under MNREGA and Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali Yojana, supporting both irrigation and ecology. These parallel efforts ensure that growth spreads evenly, not just within the city but across the district.

Why It Matters: Patna’s Image Is Changing

This transformation is more than construction—it’s confidence in motion. For years, Patna has battled the stereotype of being “slow to grow.” Now, these projects show a city stepping into its own, ready to attract investors, students, and entrepreneurs.

Every bridge, road, and zone adds a layer of pride. And as these developments unfold, they redefine Bihar’s identity on the national map—not as a story of catching up, but of leading ahead.

Article Title: Patna Municipal Corporation Launches Massive Anti-Dengue Drive
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A City at War — And Everyone’s Involved

Every dawn in Patna now begins with action. Streets echo with the hum of fogging machines, and residents watch as civic workers spray every corner. The Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC), under the leadership of Municipal Commissioner Yashpal Meena, has launched a war-level anti-dengue drive, reaching 18,000 homes daily.

Unlike previous seasonal clean-ups, this mission is intense, structured, and city-wide. Teams are not only eliminating larvae but also spreading awareness door-to-door. The aim is clear — stop dengue before it starts.

Coordinated Effort: 375 Teams, Two Shifts, One Goal

To ensure complete coverage, five anti-larva teams have been deployed in every ward. In high-risk dengue areas, ten special units now work round the clock. The teams check rooftops, pots, overhead tanks, and under-construction sites — all potential breeding spots.

Across 75 municipal wards, 375 teams operate in two shifts daily. They use Temephos for larva control and Malathion for fogging. Meanwhile, a special 500-metre perimeter is sprayed around every dengue-positive home identified by the health department.

This coordinated rhythm of inspection, fogging, and verification ensures that no neighbourhood is left behind.

Hospitals on High Alert

Hospitals, often overlooked breeding grounds, are receiving special focus. Dedicated workers visit PMCH, NMCH, AIIMS, IGIMS, IGIC, Gardiner Hospital, and Rajvanshi Nagar Hospital daily for spraying and fogging.

This hospital-level vigilance reduces infection risk for patients and frontline workers. Moreover, it prevents re-infestation from within high-traffic healthcare zones — a crucial step that strengthens Patna’s overall defence.

Vehicles, Zones, and Rapid Response

The civic body has also mobilised 57 fogging vehicles across six major zones:

Pataliputra Zone – 13 vehicles Nutan Rajdhani Zone – 12 vehicles Azimabad Zone – 7 vehicles Patna City Zone – 6 vehicles Kankarbagh Zone – 10 vehicles Bankipur Zone – 9 vehicles

If residents face issues, they can call toll-free number 155304, and a rapid-response unit reaches the location the same day. This real-time grievance redressal has made citizens active partners in the drive.

From Awareness to Action

While PMC’s machinery is vast, the true strength lies in citizen cooperation. Commissioner Yashpal Meena repeatedly urges residents to keep their surroundings clean and water-free. Stagnant water, even in a bottle cap, can become a breeding ground within days.

Therefore, small daily habits — covering tanks, cleaning trays, and removing puddles — directly reduce dengue risk. Additionally, responding to fogging teams and sharing feedback builds trust and helps improve the process.

Together, these collective actions transform awareness into sustained prevention.

Article Title: AIIMS Patna Doctors Remove 3.1 Kg Spleen From Six-Year-Old in Rare Surgery
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Miracle in Patna: AIIMS Doctors Remove 3.1 Kg Spleen From Six-Year-Old Boy in Record Surgery

Patna, November 4, 2025 — A six-year-old boy weighing just 18 kilograms carried a 3.1 kg spleen inside his tiny body. It sounds unbelievable, yet doctors at AIIMS Patna turned this medical crisis into a story of strength, skill, and hope.

When a Rare Disease Meets Unbreakable Spirit

The boy arrived at AIIMS Patna with a swollen abdomen and constant infections. After several tests, doctors found he had Gaucher’s disease, a rare genetic disorder. This condition occurs when the body lacks an enzyme called glucocerebrosidase, causing fatty deposits in organs such as the spleen and liver.

Over time, his spleen expanded to a shocking 30 by 20 centimetres, weighing 3.1 kilograms. It began pressing on other organs, threatening his life. At that point, surgery became the only option.

However, operating on a young child with such an enlarged spleen posed a massive challenge. Still, the AIIMS Patna team stepped up fearlessly.

The Expert Team Behind the Record-Breaking Surgery

The complex procedure was led by Dr. Amit Kumar and Dr. Amit Kumar Sinha from the Department of Paediatric Surgery. They were joined by Dr. Rashi, Dr. Digamber, Dr. Gaurav, and Dr. Saurav, who worked tirelessly to ensure precision at every step.

Meanwhile, Dr. Neeraj Kumar guided the anaesthesia team with steady expertise. Dr. Pratap Patra, a senior paediatrician, monitored the boy’s pre- and post-surgery condition carefully.

Together, these doctors turned an impossible case into a milestone in Indian paediatric surgery. The 3.1 kg spleen removal from a child of this age now stands as a record across the country.

From Pain to Recovery: A Turning Point for Bihar’s Healthcare

The surgery lasted several hours, but every second was worth it. The boy recovered smoothly and was discharged in a stable condition. His parents, once worried beyond measure, now call it a second chance at life.

This operation proves that Bihar’s healthcare system is evolving rapidly. Families no longer need to travel outside the state for high-risk surgeries. With experts like these, AIIMS Patna continues to strengthen faith in Bihar’s medical excellence.

AIIMS Patna: Shaping the Future of Child Healthcare

AIIMS Patna has become a symbol of hope and progress in eastern India. Each breakthrough reminds us that world-class care is possible right here in Bihar.

This surgery is not just a medical success — it’s a message of confidence to every family seeking advanced treatment locally. As Bihar’s healthcare infrastructure grows stronger, stories like these redefine how the world views the state’s capabilities.
