Article Title: Discover how NIOS and IHCNBT are reviving Nalanda’s legacy in modern education
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Echoes of Nalanda: Where Ancient Wisdom Meets Modern Minds

Centuries before global universities existed, Nalanda stood tall as a beacon of knowledge and intellectual freedom. Today, its legacy is making a comeback — not as ruins of the past, but as a living philosophy reshaping modern education in India.

The roots of monastic learning stretch back to Buddhist viharas from the 5th century BCE. These early centers of meditation soon became structured institutions teaching ethics, philosophy, and logic. Over time, renowned universities like Nalanda, Vikramashila, and Takshashila became magnets for scholars across Asia. Their approach was holistic — valuing moral discipline, intellectual debate, and lifelong learning — qualities still vital for modern classrooms.

Nalanda: The World’s First Multidisciplinary University

While earlier monasteries focused mainly on spiritual growth, Nalanda Mahavihara (5th–12th century CE) broke new ground. It offered a residential, organized, and secular curriculum that taught grammar, medicine, astronomy, mathematics, and the arts alongside Buddhist philosophy.

What made Nalanda revolutionary was its inclusive and dialogic learning model. Debates, discussions, and commentaries were central to its pedagogy. Students came from China, Korea, Tibet, and Southeast Asia — a true example of global education before globalization. Education here wasn’t about sectarianism; it was a pursuit of universal enlightenment blending faith and reason.

Modern Revival: NIOS and IHCNBT Bring Monastic Learning into the National Framework

In the spirit of Nalanda, the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS), in collaboration with the Indian Himalayan Council of Nalanda Buddhist Tradition (IHCNBT), has launched a landmark initiative. Their mission? To modernize and formally recognize monastic education across India.

Traditionally conducted in Bhoti, this system preserves Buddhist teachings and classical Indian literature — from Nagarjuna and Dharmakirti to timeless Sanskrit works like Ramayana and Meghaduta. Now, this intellectual treasure is being aligned with modern academic frameworks at the Elementary, Secondary, and Senior Secondary levels.

Rajeev Kumar Singh, Director (Academics) at NIOS, calls it “a bridge between ancient wisdom and modern opportunity.” He emphasizes that the initiative is not about secularizing Buddhism but about empowering learners and giving equal recognition to traditional knowledge in today’s education system.

Preserving Culture, Strengthening Identity

The IHCNBT, representing Buddhist communities across Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and North Bengal, plays a pivotal role in this educational renaissance. For Maling Gombu, General Secretary of IHCNBT, the initiative is both patriotic and cultural. It strengthens India’s identity as the birthplace of great learning traditions and ensures that monasteries remain active centers of knowledge.

Today, 132 monasteries across the Himalayas have been accredited by NIOS, enrolling nearly 10,000 learners. This movement is not just an administrative reform — it’s a cultural revival. The Bodh Darshan initiative dignifies centuries-old Himalayan education systems, reaffirming India’s position as the spiritual and intellectual cradle of Buddhist thought.

Nalanda’s Spirit Lives On

As the world searches for balance between technology and wisdom, Nalanda’s philosophy offers a timeless solution — education that nourishes both intellect and soul. Its revival through NIOS and IHCNBT is more than policy; it’s a return to India’s roots in value-based, inclusive learning.

SVSU’s mission is not just to provide certificates—it aims to build career-ready and entrepreneurial youth. Each course aligns with the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF), ensuring national-level credibility and recognition.

Equally important, the university is transforming how people view vocational education in India. It is proving that skill-based learning can be as prestigious as traditional higher education.

What Bihar Stands to Gain

Firstly, Bihar has a young population full of ambition but limited by traditional education paths. The new skill university will give them a direct gateway to employability and innovation.

Secondly, industry-integrated education will help reduce the mismatch between academic learning and job requirements. Students will no longer struggle to find work after graduation—they will already be part of it.

Article Title: WCDC Chief and ADRI Researchers Call for Modern Career Pathways for Bihar’s Women
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A New Wave of Voices in Patna

Patna woke up to a powerful message this week: Bihar’s women deserve careers beyond the narrow lanes of “stereotyped” work. At an ADRI panel discussion in the city on November 20, 2025, WCDC Managing Director Bandana Preyashi strongly urged the state to act faster and smarter. Her words created a moment that hit both the mind and the heart.

She said women still get pushed toward the same old roles. Beauty work. Tailoring. Basic support jobs. However, their dreams now stretch far wider. Many want modern roles like computer operators, digital service providers, and office administrators. They want dignity, skill, and a future.

The Core Issue: Skills Are Missing, Not Aspirations

Preyashi explained the real problem. Women want to grow. The government wants them to dream big. Yet the skill gap blocks their journey. As a result, they cannot reach the jobs they truly want.She framed it bluntly: “We haven’t been able to help women realise the very aspirations we ask them to seek.”

This gap restricts thousands of marginalised women who want dignified and better-paid work. And this is exactly where Bihar must step up with urgency.

New Research Reveals a Hidden Pattern

The event began with a joint research presentation by ADRI and the University of Reading (@UniofReading).Dr. Ashmita Gupta (@ADRI_Official) highlighted an important pattern. She said aspirations in Bihar still depend heavily on gender, caste and exposure. Wages matter, but not as much as many assume. Because of limited awareness, people mainly hope for jobs they hear about often — especially uniformed roles or government posts.

This insight surprised many attendees, yet it also opened the door for deeper conversations.

Why Limited Exposure Shapes Dreams

Professor Kambhampati (@UniofReading) added a strong perspective. She explained that people can aspire only to what they understand. When women lack exposure, they cannot imagine possibilities beyond their neighbourhoods.

She described it simply:“To aspire, you must first know what the ideal looks like and how to reach it.”

Therefore, expanding awareness becomes as important as giving training. Without both, Bihar will continue to see restricted ambitions, especially among women.

A Room Full of Changemakers

The panel also included Prem Prakash (NITI Aayog Bihar), Dr. Sunita Lall, and Dr. Ushasi Gupta. Academics, students, civil society members and policymakers filled the room. Because of their shared concern, the discussion grew energetic and solution-focused.

Everyone agreed that if Bihar wants a stronger labour market, it must close the ambition gap. It must also improve access to non-traditional work pathways. Most importantly, it must give women the skills and exposure that unlock modern careers.

The Bigger Picture for Bihar’s Future

This conversation signals something bigger. Bihar is rewriting its story every day. Women stand at the centre of that transformation. However, they still need a bridge — a bridge connecting dreams with opportunities.

When Bihar expands training, breaks stereotypes and celebrates modern careers, women rise. And when women rise, families rise. Entire communities rise. Ultimately, the state rises.

Article Title: Bihar Introduces New 2025 Renewable Tariff Regulations
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
A New Chapter Begins for Bihar’s Renewable Energy Future

Bihar has taken a bold step. The Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission (BERC) has rolled out the 2025 Terms and Conditions for Tariff Determination from Renewable Energy Sources Regulations, and the shift is already creating conversations in the clean-energy sector. These rules aim to bring order, clarity, and confidence into how renewable tariffs are set. As a result, the framework now supports developers, protects consumers, and aligns Bihar with India’s national clean-energy goals.

The Commission created these regulations using the powers granted under the Electricity Act, 2003. This Act encourages renewable expansion and mandates a minimum renewable share in the state’s energy mix. Because of this, the new rules stand on strong legal ground and reflect the state’s intention to scale green energy with consistency and accountability.

Why These 2025 Regulations Matter More Than Ever

Bihar is changing fast. The demand for reliable and affordable clean power continues to grow. Therefore, a predictable tariff system becomes essential. BERC already holds the responsibility of setting tariffs for generation, supply, transmission, and wheeling. Now, with the 2025 rules, the Commission adds sharper structure to the renewable roadmap.

Developers often struggle with unpredictability. Investors worry about financial clarity. Consumers want fair tariffs. Interestingly, these regulations address each of these concerns in a balanced way.

Ceiling Levelized Tariff: A Game-Changer for Tariff Stability

One of the strongest features of the 2025 rules appears in Clause 65, which introduces the ceiling levelized tariff. This tariff acts as the maximum cap for renewable projects. Because of this, developers can plan better while consumers receive protection from unusually high tariffs.

This ceiling improves financial modelling, encourages disciplined pricing, and builds trust. In fact, it also allows long-term planning in a sector that previously dealt with major uncertainties.

Aligning Bihar With National Renewable Priorities

Policies evolve quickly in clean energy. So, Clause 66 ensures that any central or state policy from the Ministry of Power, MNRE, or the Bihar Government automatically takes precedence in case of conflicts. This alignment prevents regulatory confusion and keeps Bihar’s energy reforms on the same track as India’s national clean-energy mission.

Moreover, it keeps policy implementation smooth and avoids overlapping guidelines that slow down project progress.

Flexibility, Transparency, and Built-In Corrective Mechanisms

No regulation can predict everything. Because of this, BERC added flexibility through Clause 67, which allows the Commission to relax provisions when genuine difficulties arise. It must provide reasons in writing and hear affected parties. As a result, stakeholder concerns receive space within the system.

Additionally, Clause 68 helps remove implementation challenges through formal orders. This prevents delays in project execution and ensures small roadblocks do not slow major renewable initiatives.

To stay relevant, Clause 69 empowers BERC to amend the regulations whenever needed. The sector evolves fast. Therefore, rules must evolve too.

Finally, Clause 70 officially repeals the older 2017 regulations, allowing Bihar to operate under a refreshed, modern, and future-ready renewable tariff framework.

Bihar’s Renewable Push Is More Than Regulation — It’s a Vision

These rules signal more than administrative updates. They reflect Bihar’s ambition to build a cleaner, stable, and investor-friendly power sector. The state is moving into a new era where renewable energy becomes central to growth instead of an optional alternative.

Article Title: Singhada:The Superfood That Boosts Immunity, Beauty & Everyday Energy

Water chestnuts contain more than 70% water. This high water content keeps the body hydrated even when winter dryness increases. They also offer fibre, potassium, manganese, copper, vitamin C, sodium, and vitamin B6.These nutrients support metabolism, improve digestion, and maintain energy throughout the day.

Moreover, the fruit remains low in calories and almost fat-free. Because of this, many fitness-focused individuals choose it as a guilt-free winter snack. It keeps you full for longer and prevents unnecessary munching.

Singhada naturally supports weight control. It fills the stomach without adding extra calories. As a result, it reduces overeating and helps maintain a balanced lifestyle.The fibre in water chestnuts also supports smooth digestion. It prevents constipation and keeps the gut clean, which becomes even more important during winter when physical activity often reduces.

Additionally, people with diabetes benefit greatly from this winter fruit. Its low glycaemic index ensures it does not spike blood sugar levels. It also supports stable blood pressure because potassium and sodium help regulate heart function. This becomes crucial in winter months when many people experience sudden pressure fluctuations.

Immunity, Skin Glow & Detox Support — All in One Seasonal Fruit

Water chestnuts strengthen the immune system naturally. Their vitamin C content boosts the body’s resistance against infections, colds, and coughs.Furthermore, their antioxidant properties help flush out toxins. As a result, skin stays soft, hydrated, and glowing. Regular consumption also reduces winter dryness.

Because of this, many families in Bihar include singhada in their daily meals during the cold season. It works as a beauty booster, a digestive friend, and an immunity shield — all at the same time.

A Simple Fruit With Endless Goodness

In simple words, singhada is a winter blessing. It keeps the body hydrated, supports better digestion, lowers blood pressure, manages blood sugar, and enhances skin health. You can enjoy it raw, boiled, or in delicious winter recipes. And each bite brings you closer to a healthier winter.

When storms destroy fields, hope usually collapses with them. But this time, Bihar’s farmers are rising again — stronger and united — with a new relief grant that brings real support straight to their homes.

Montha Cyclone: A Storm That Shook Lives

Cyclone Montha didn’t just bring rain.It brought fear, loss, and uncertainty.

The storm tore through Odisha, West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Bihar, damaging ripe paddy crops and flooding fields right before the Rabi season. Farmers watched their year-long efforts drown in waterlogged fields. Many feared they wouldn’t recover before the next harvest cycle.

Yet, when reports from district officers confirmed the massive losses, the new Bihar government moved quickly. And finally, after days of waiting, the relief window opened.

The Relief Plan: Direct Support That Reaches Farmers

Now, affected farmers can apply for Agriculture Input Subsidy–2025, which covers 12 districts, 39 blocks, and 397 panchayats.This is not just compensation — it is recovery support.

The subsidy rates are simple and farmer-friendly:

Article Title: Bihar Fixes 227 Black Spots: Mega Road Safety Plan to Reduce Accidents
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
When a state takes road safety as seriously as Bihar does today, change doesn’t just begin — it accelerates.

Bihar’s Mega Plan to Reduce Road Accidents

Road safety has become a top priority for the Bihar Government. As accident numbers started raising concern, authorities acted fast and launched a targeted mission to locate and fix every dangerous point on the road network. As a result, teams identified 285 Black Spots across the state in the last three years. They didn’t stop there. They fixed 227 locations, and work on the remaining ones is already underway.

Transportation officials shared an encouraging update. The Road Construction Department improved 93 out of 96 spots in 2022, 92 out of 96 in 2023, and 42 out of 93 in 2024. The remaining 58 spots will see complete correction by the end of this year. This pace signals the beginning of a safer Bihar, road by road.

National Highways: A Massive Improvement Drive

The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has also moved swiftly. They identified 260 Black Spots on highways based on standards of the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways. They improved all 260. Additionally, Bihar’s own standards helped detect 563 more Black Spots, and 547 locations already received safety upgrades. Only 16 Black Spots remain under improvement, and work continues with urgency.

These numbers show a focused and aggressive effort. The state wants to ensure that highways become safer for everyone — bus passengers, truck drivers, daily commuters, and long-distance travelers.

Rural Roads: No Black Spots, Only Six Grey Zones

Interestingly, the Rural Works Department did not identify any Black Spot on rural roads. Yet they detected six Grey Spots in Madhubani, Muzaffarpur, Buxar, and Kaimur. Teams corrected all six and reopened them for public use. These quick actions reduced risks where villagers travel daily.

Black Spot vs Grey Spot: Understanding the Difference

A Black Spot is a road location where frequent accidents and deaths occur regularly. Tight curves, poor visibility, faulty design, potholes, or dark stretches often cause repeated crashes.

A Grey Spot indicates a place where severe injuries happen often, even if fatalities remain low. Both categories need attention. Bihar is now addressing both with equal seriousness.

Government’s Renewed Focus on Road Safety

Bihar’s Transport Minister, Shrawan Kumar, emphasised the government’s commitment. He said the state continues to correct every risky location and will soon fix the remaining ones. Authorities are also mapping new danger points. Once identified, they will improve them without delay.

His statement shows intent. More importantly, the progress shows action.

A Safer Bihar Is Taking Shape

The combined efforts of NHAI, the Road Construction Department, and the Rural Works Department reveal one clear message — Bihar is building safer roads for its people. This mission matters because each corrected Black Spot means one less danger zone and one more life potentially saved.

Article Title: Purnea Airport to Connect with NH-31:Committee Formed for DPR

NH-31 serves as a vital economic corridor.Therefore, linking it directly to Purnea Airport strengthens regional access.

At present, airport connectivity limits travel efficiency.However, the new road link could reduce delays significantly.In addition, it may boost tourism, trade, and emergency mobility.

Most importantly, North Bihar gains smoother access to national air routes.Consequently, businesses and investors may look at Purnea differently.

Committee Formed to Drive the DPR Process

To ensure structured execution, the administration formed a multi-departmental committee.This committee will oversee surveys, planning, and coordination.

The Executive Engineer, Purnea Road Division, received clear instructions.He must submit a detailed survey report for the proposed link road.Meanwhile, the committee will monitor progress at every stage.

Article Title: Bihar Enters Top 10 Egg Producing States

From Breakfast Plates to National Charts: How Bihar Quietly Became India’s New Egg Powerhouse

Bihar’s Egg Story Is No Longer Small. It’s National.

For decades, Bihar was known mainly as a consumer of eggs.However, that image has now changed—decisively and confidently.

In a major milestone, Bihar has entered India’s top 10 egg-producing states.More importantly, this shift reflects grassroots growth, not overnight luck.

According to Animal Husbandry Statistics 2023–24 under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Bihar’s rise is both measurable and meaningful.As a result, the state is no longer standing on the sidelines of India’s poultry economy.

Three Times Growth in Just Nine Years

To understand the scale, the numbers speak clearly.

In 2014–15, Bihar produced 9,845 lakh eggs.By 2023–24, production surged to 34,401 lakh eggs.

That means Bihar tripled its output in less than a decade.Meanwhile, this growth outpaced the national average.

Consequently, Bihar’s entry into the top 10 is not symbolic.Instead, it signals structural transformation.

Traditionally dominant states like Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, West Bengal, Karnataka, and Maharashtra still lead.However, Bihar’s inclusion proves the gap is narrowing.

Earlier, Bihar relied heavily on egg imports from other states.Now, the state is steadily building its own supply strength.

As a result, farmers earn more locally.At the same time, supply chains shorten and prices stabilize.

First, poultry farming expanded rapidly in rural Bihar.Small farmers adopted modern practices with lower entry costs.

Second, the Mukhyamantri Poultry Development Scheme played a key role.Through this, the government offered subsidies, training, and financial support.

Meanwhile, rising egg consumption across Bihar created steady demand.Consequently, producers felt secure investing more.

Article Title: Bihar Factories Double in 19 Years: A Positive Shift in Industrial Growth
Author: Amrita
Main Body Content:
Bihar’s Factories Have Doubled—A Quiet Industrial Comeback Is Taking Shape

Bihar is building again.Slowly, steadily, and with renewed confidence.

For years, the state stayed away from India’s industrial spotlight. However, fresh data now tells a different story. Bihar is not standing still anymore. Instead, it is laying the foundation for long-term industrial growth.

According to the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) 2023–24, the number of registered factories in Bihar has doubled over the last 19 years. Clearly, this growth reflects a changing economic mindset. More importantly, it signals resilience, recovery, and rising ambition.

A Steady Rise That Signals Structural Change

In 2004–05, Bihar had 1,674 registered factories.Gradually, the number increased.

By 2010–11, it reached 2,805 units.Later, in 2018–19, it touched 3,422 factories.

Then came the pandemic. Like everywhere else, industries faced disruption. Even so, Bihar showed recovery strength. In 2022–23, factories stood at 3,307. Soon after, in 2023–24, the number rose to 3,386, recording a 2.4% annual growth.

Therefore, despite challenges, the growth curve remains upward. That itself speaks volumes.

Bihar’s Position Is Improving on the National Map

Across India, 2,60,061 factories operated in 2023–24. Within this landscape, Bihar’s presence is becoming more visible.

Notably, Bihar has moved ahead of Jharkhand (2,889) and Odisha (3,281) in factory count. This shift highlights consistent improvement. At the same time, it shows how eastern India’s industrial balance is evolving.

While larger states still lead, Bihar’s progress proves that industrial revival does not happen overnight. Instead, it grows layer by layer.

Regional Gains Reflect Growing Industrial Confidence

Surpassing neighbouring states marks a confidence boost.Moreover, it reflects improving policy focus.

States like Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal currently have higher factory numbers. However, Bihar’s advantage lies in its emerging sectors and untapped potential. Therefore, the state stands at a promising inflection point.

With the right push, Bihar can convert momentum into scale.

Emerging Sectors Are Powering the Next Phase

According to Ram Lal Khetan, President of the Bihar Industries Association, eastern India is entering a new industrial phase. Bihar, in particular, holds strong promise.

Currently, sectors such as food processing, packaging, plastics, mineral-based industries, and apparel manufacturing are expanding steadily. Importantly, small and medium enterprises are leading this change.

Meanwhile, improvements in logistics, energy supply, land access, and skill development can accelerate this progress even further.

Factories, Jobs, and a New Economic Narrative

Every new factory adds more than numbers.It creates jobs.It boosts local supply chains.It strengthens confidence.

Therefore, Bihar’s industrial rise is not just about rankings. Instead, it is about opportunity spreading across districts. With sustained reforms and investments, the state’s manufacturing ecosystem can scale faster.

The direction is clear. The foundation is visible. The momentum is real.
